units.slavonic_incipit: Стра́нничество безчлове́чное полꙋчи́хъ, и҆ па́сти свинїѧ̀
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: странничество безчловечное получих и пасти свиния осужден бых
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Тропа́рь:* Стра́нничество безчлове́чное полꙋчи́хъ, и҆ па́сти свинїѧ̀ ѡ҆сꙋжде́нъ бы́хъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ моѐ расточи́хъ бога́тство, є҆́же млⷭ҇тивнѡ въ ско́рѣ пода́лъ є҆сѝ, и҆ бы́хъ ѿ всѣ́хъ на́гъ. но ты̀ ꙗ҆́кѡ бг҃ъ мо́й оу҆ще́дри:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* Inhuman sojourning was my lot, and I was condemned to feed swine, for I squandered my wealth which Thou didst mercifully and promptly grant, and I became stripped of all things; but do Thou, as my God, have compassion upon me!

units.slavonic_incipit: Не и҆ма́мъ дерзнове́нїѧ чл҃вѣколю́бче, возрѣ́ти и҆
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: не имам дерзновения члвеколюбче возрети и видети согрешив
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Тропа́рь:* Не и҆ма́мъ дерзнове́нїѧ чл҃вѣколю́бче, возрѣ́ти и҆ ви́дѣти, согрѣши́въ на нб҃о безмѣ́рнꙋю высотꙋ̀, ни нарещи́сѧ сы́нъ тво́й блꙋ́дный. но оу҆ще́дри мѧ̀ то́не и҆мѣ́ѧй безмѣ́рнꙋю млⷭ҇ть:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* I have no boldness, O Lover of mankind, to look up and behold the boundless height of heaven, having sinned against heaven, nor to be called Thy prodigal son; but have compassion upon me, Thou Who alone possessest boundless mercy!

units.slavonic_incipit: Несказа́нное ти ржⷭ҇тво̀, и҆ неизрече́нный рожества́
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: несказанное ти ржтво и неизреченный рожества ти образ
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Бг҃оро́диченъ:* Несказа́нное ти ржⷭ҇тво̀, и҆ неизрече́нный рожества́ ти ѡ҆́бразъ Дб҃це, ꙗ҆́кѡ бг҃а вы́ше оу҆ма̀ ражда́еши, дѣ́вство нескве́рненое и҆мꙋ́щи. тѣ́мъ тѧ̀ всѝ и҆́стиннꙋю бц҃ꙋ, досто́йнѡ сла́вимъ:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Theotokion:* Unutterable is thy giving-birth, and ineffable is the manner of thy conceiving, O Mistress, for thou bearest God beyond all understanding while preserving undefiled virginity; therefore, we all worthily glorify thee as the true Mother of God!

units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Бг҃оро́диченъ:* Бꙋ́ди ми всечⷭ҇таѧ Влⷣчце, тишина̀ и҆ приста́нище оу҆тѣше́нїѧ, преводѧ́щее къ бж҃твенномꙋ бре́гꙋ небла́ема, бꙋ́ри страсте́й мои́хъ оу҆кроти́вши:

units.slavonic_incipit: *Конта́кїонъ. Гла́съ д҃:* Нн҃ѣ вре́мѧ дѣ́лателное
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: контакион глас д нне время делателное вися при
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Конта́кїонъ. Гла́съ д҃:* Нн҃ѣ вре́мѧ дѣ́лателное ꙗ҆ви́сѧ, при две́рехъ сꙋ́дъ, воста́немъ оу҆́бѡ постѧ́щесѧ. принесе́мъ сле́зы оу҆миле́нїѧ мл҃твами зовꙋ́ще: согрѣши́хѡмъ па́че пѣска̀ мо́рскагѡ. но ѡ҆сла́би содѣ́телю всѣ́хъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ да прїи́мемъ нетлѣ́нныѧ вѣнца̀:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Kontakion, Tone 4:* Now the time for action has appeared; judgment is at the doors; let us arise, therefore, fasting; let us offer tears of compunction with prayers, crying out: We have sinned more than the sand of the sea; but remit our sins, O Creator of all, that we may receive incorruptible crowns!

units.slavonic_incipit: *Ст҃мꙋ, Конта́кїонъ. Гла́съ и҆, По́добенъ: Взбра́нной:*
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: стму контакион глас и подобен взбранной премудрости сщенный
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Ст҃мꙋ, Конта́кїонъ. Гла́съ и҆, По́добенъ: Взбра́нной:* Премꙋ́дрости сщ҃енный и҆ бж҃твенный ѻ҆рга́нъ, бг҃осло́вїѧ свѣ́тлꙋю согла́снѡ трꙋбꙋ̀, воспѣва́емъ тѧ Григѡ́рїе бг҃осло́ве. Но ꙗ҆́кѡ оу҆́мъ Оу҆мꙋ̀ пе́рвомꙋ предстоѧ́й, к не́мꙋ оу҆́мъ на́шъ оу҆пра́ви, да зове́мъ Ра́дꙋйсѧ проповѣ́дниче бл҃гти:
units.english_cohort_translation: *To the Saint, Kontakion, Tone 8, Podoben: "To thee, the Champion Leader" (Взбра́нной):* As the sacred and divine instrument of wisdom, and the harmonious, luminous trumpet of theology, we praise thee, O Gregory, theologian. But as a mind standing before the First Mind, direct our mind unto Him, that we may cry: Rejoice, O preacher of grace!

units.slavonic_incipit: Се́й бж҃е́ственныѧ и҆ без̾вечернѧѧ и҆мѣ́ѧщеи свѣ́тлости
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: сей бжественныя и безвечерняя имеящеи светлости сын правдивый
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Се́й бж҃е́ственныѧ и҆ без̾вечернѧѧ и҆мѣ́ѧщеи свѣ́тлости Сы́нъ, правди́вый правди́вагѡ бг҃а чл҃къ, и҆ чꙋдо́вный бж҃скихъ спра́въ слꙋжи́тель и҆ дѣ́латель, ѿчи́знꙋ въ пра́вдѣ мѣ́лъ мѣ́сто надъ всѣ́ми мѣ́стами царство́ючее, а҆ роди́телєвъ за́цныхъ и҆ сла́вныхъ, кото́рїи є҆гѡ̀ не позвѣ́рхо́вне то́лко и҆ водлꙋ́гъ змы́слености члове́кои, а҆ле дале́кѡ ба́рзѣй внꙋ́трне и҆ неви́домымъ, цно́тою и҆ навꙋ́кою приѡздо́бити стара́лисѧ. Гды́ те́ды є҆мꙋ̀ ба́рзо молоды́хъ лѣ́техъ бꙋ́дꙋчемꙋ ѿте́цъ скончи́лсѧ, ма́тка та́къ є҆го̀ само́го, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆ бра́тїю є҆го̀ и҆ се́стры в навꙋ́цѣ и҆ Зако́нѣ гдⷭ҇немъ та́кже в сто́мъ пи́смѣ вы́кормила и҆ вы́ховала, и҆ того̀ кото́рый позвѣ́рховноѣ мꙋ́дрости межъ оу҆чи́телми навыка́лъ, до́брѣ цѣни́ти оу҆мѣ́ла. кото́рый ѡ҆стрости прирожо́ного довтѣ́пꙋ, пи́лност в навꙋ́цѣ взае́мне зєдночи́вши, в мало́мъ ча́сѣ всеѣ логї́ческоѣ навы́къ оу҆мѣ́етности. А҆ гды́ былъ въ два́дцати лѣ́техъ, всѣ́ собѣ̀ ре́чи на землѝ взга́ржоныи, и҆ на́ конъ ба́рзѣй ѡ҆шꙋкава́телными почитны́вши, шꙋка́лъ оу҆течи́сѧ и҆ оу҆да́ти до причи́нци и҆ пода́вцы все́й мꙋ́дрости бг҃а, и҆ пре́зъ живо́тъ доскона́лшїй, себѐ всего̀ ѻ҆́номꙋ ца́ло ѡ҆фѣрова́ти. Ѡко́лъ то́тъ це́ль и҆ предєвзѧ́тє своѐ ѿкрыва́етъ бг҃олне́ннои ма́тцѣ свое́й и҆ ба́рзо велико́е к бг҃ꙋ ро́скоха́нєсѧ и҆ роспа́ленꙋю любо́въ. кото́рꙋю та́кже зна́йде́етъ, а҆чколвекъ долгоболѣ́знꙋю, є҆днакъ ро́вне з ни́мъ з того̀ ра́дꙋютисѧ. Наты́хмѣстъ те́ды ма́тка дѣ́ти, кото́рыи былѝ з нею̀ згрома́дивши, и҆ што́ и҆ дѣ́ти, з весе́лемъ ре́кши, кото́рїи ми далъ бг҃ъ, и҆ зда́нѧ и҆́хъ досвѣ́дчала кото́рое мѣ́ли ѡ҆ добро́мъ, и҆ вели́кого цель и҆ предєвзѧ́тє и҆́мъ ѿкрыва́етъ. Ѻ҆́нъ те́жъ напомина́лныхъ сло́въ до ни́хъ зажи́вши, рыхлѣ́й є҆́жли вы́мовитїсѧ мо́жетъ, всѣ́хъ и҆́хъ намо́вленыхъ и҆ навче́ныхъ ѡ҆держа́лъ, и҆зъ оу҆се́рдїемъ оу҆тѣка́ючїхъ з того̀ живо́та, а҆ и҆дꙋ́чихъ до подо́бнои є҆мꙋ̀ любвѐ къ бг҃ꙋ. Для то́го те́жъ и҆ має́тность ᲂу҆бѡ́гимъ по Є҆ѵ҃лїю̀ розда́вши, ща́стє и҆ добро́є мѣ́нє Ца́рское, и҆ че́сти, и҆ похва́лы в дома́хъ Кроле́вскихъ ве́село и҆ до́брымъ срⷵцемъ зоста́вивши, шо́лъ за хрⷭ҇томъ. Ма́тку те́ды и҆ Се́стры к Монастырꙋ̀ Дѣви́чымъ постанови́вши, Бра́тїю за́сь з собо́ю вза́вши, на Го́рꙋ сто́сти тезоимени́тꙋю встꙋпи́лъ. А҆́ле бра́тїи намовля́етъ а҆́бы въ дрꙋги́хъ Монастыре́хъ преме́шкова́ли, и҆ за несдаре́нємъ ча́сꙋ зєдноти́вшисѧ є҆де́нъ з дрꙋги́мъ, живо́тъ бг҃ꙋ пра́вова́дили, а҆ себѐ само́го в послꙋше́нство и҆ спра́вова́нє чꙋдо́вногѡ є҆дногѡ мꙋ́жа ве́длꙋгъ ти́хогѡ и҆ молчали́вогѡ живота̀, само́мꙋ кꙋ̀ живо́тꙋ тогѡ̀ ѡ҆дає́тъ, и҆́менемъ Никоди́мови: ѿ кото́рогѡ вшеля́когѡ приказа́нѧ бж҃ского, вшеля́кои цно́ты в поко́рности дꙋше́внои са́мымъ скꙋ́ткомъ навчи́вшисѧ, и҆ Всест҃о́и бц҃и застꙋпле́нїе и҆ ѡ҆боро́нꙋ къ всѣ̑мъ ре́чамъ незва́лченꙋю и҆ непрела́манꙋю въ ѡ҆бѧ́вленїи та́емномъ та́мъ принѧ́вши, по ѡ҆́ногѡ ꙗ҆́жъ до бг҃а ѿше́стїи. И҆ въ вели́кои Ла́ѵрѣ лѣ́тъ ко́лко переме́шкавши, з ба́рзо вели́кою ѡ҆хо́тою, и҆ дозрѣ́лымъ и҆ доскона́лымъ ро́зꙋмомъ, ми́лости ти́хогѡ и҆ молчали́вогѡ живота̀. ѿ Ла́ѵры выхо́дитъ, и҆ до пꙋсты́ни любо́вне встꙋпа́етъ, и҆ любо́въ бж҃їю за́вше до любвѝ приклада́ючи, и҆ в срⷵцꙋ свое́мъ помина́ючи, нє̀ бм҃ъ оу҆ста́вичне поспо́лꙋ жи́ти всѣ̑мъ срⷵцемъ пожада́ючи, на ѡ҆ста́тнєє сро́гоє цвиче́нє себѐ выдає́тъ. И҆ ѡ҆па́трности ѡ҆сторо́жнои з ѡ҆бѣ́хъ сторо́нъ змы́слы своє̀ повита́гнꙋвши, и҆ до скро́мности привѣ́кши, а҆ к бг҃ꙋ мы́сль свою̀ и҆ ро́зꙋмъ повы́шивъши, и҆ ча́съ весь на мл҃твахъ и҆ бг҃омы́слености заба́вивши, и҆ живо́тъ спорѧди́вши свои̑ превыбо́рне, бѣсо́вскїи ко́йны по́мочꙋ бж҃ею, до ща́дꙋ звытѧ́жаєтъ, и҆ всено́чнымъ стоѧ́ньемъ пре жро́дла сле́зъ дꙋшꙋ̀ ѡ҆чи́стивши, начи́нїемъ выбо́рнымъ да́рѡвъ бж҃твеннагѡ дх҃а зоста́лъ, и҆ бж҃скїи зъѧвле́нѧ ча́стыи, и҆ нема́лъ оу҆ста́вичныи вида́лъ. А҆ што̀ чꙋдовнѣ́йшаѧ, и҆́жъ и҆ прехоже́на пре неима́нїтїскїи навѣ̑ти и҆ вта́рчки, до Ѳессалони́ки, и҆ до Ски́тꙋ в Ве́ррїи бꙋдꙋчого ѿпра́вꙋючи, и҆ з нѣ́которыми мѣ́стами розмо́вꙋ мѣ́ти примꙋшаный бꙋ́дꙋчи, а҆ ни та́къ преходи́лъ з пꙋсты́нного своего̀ цвиче́нѧ сѧ, на мѣ́щскїи заба́вы. Пре лѣ́та те́ды нема́лыи доскона́ле и҆ тѣ́ло и҆ дꙋ́шꙋ ѡ҆чи́стивши, и҆ за бж҃скимъ вы́рокомъ, вели́кое пома́занє сщ҃енства принѧ́лъ, и҆ ꙗ҆́кѡ бы ꙗ҆́кїи нематерїа́лный, и҆ та́къ ре́кши, з надво́ра само́гѡ себѐ бꙋдꙋ́чїй, та́емницы тогѡ̀
units.english_cohort_translation: This son of the divine and never-waning light, a true man of the true God, and a marvelous minister and worker of divine deeds, had in truth for his homeland the city reigning over all cities [Constantinople],[^1234] and noble and renowned parents, who endeavored to adorn him not merely outwardly and according to human carnal thinking, but far more inwardly and invisibly with virtue and learning. When, therefore, while he was yet in his very early years, his father passed away, his mother nurtured and reared him, as well as his brothers and sisters, in learning and in the Law of the Lord, as also in the Holy Scriptures, and knew how to value well him who acquired outward wisdom among teachers. And having united the keenness of his natural wit with diligence in learning, in a short time he mastered all logical learning. And when he was twenty years of age, regarding all earthly things as contemptible and ultimately deceitful, he sought to flee and turn unto God, the Cause and Giver of all wisdom, and through a more perfect life to offer himself entirely and wholly unto Him. Concerning this goal and purpose, he disclosed his very great delight and burning love toward God unto his God-loving mother, whom he found, although sorrowful, yet rejoicing together with him in this. Immediately, therefore, his mother assembled the children who were with her, and saying with joy: "Behold, the children whom God has given me!" (Isa. 8:18; Heb. 2:13), she tested their disposition toward goodness, and revealed unto them the great goal and undertaking. He also addressed exhortatory words unto them, and more swiftly than can be told, he won them all over, persuaded and instructed, fleeing with zeal from this life and going forth unto a like love toward God. Therefore, having also distributed his estate unto the poor according to the Gospel (Matt. 19:21; Luke 18:22), and having left with joy and a good heart earthly fortune, the imperial estate, honors, and praises in royal courts, he followed Christ. Having, therefore, placed his mother and sisters in a convent of virgins, and taking his brothers with him, he ascended the mount eponymous with sanctity [the Holy Mountain of Athos].[^1235] Yet he persuaded his brothers to dwell in other monasteries, that, being united one with another without untimely distractions, they might direct their lives toward God; while he himself submitted to the obedience and guidance of a marvelous man according to the quiet and hesychastic life, giving himself over unto that manner of life, to a father named Nicodemus;[^1236] from whom having learned every divine commandment and every virtue in spiritual humility by actual deed, and having received there in a mystical revelation the invincible and unyielding protection and defense of the All-Holy Mother of God in all things, he remained until the elder's departure unto God. And having dwelt several years in the Great Lavra [of St. Athanasius],[^1237] with very great eagerness and mature and perfected understanding, through love for the quiet and hesychastic life he departed from the Lavra and entered lovingly into the wilderness; and ever adding divine love unto love, remembering God in his heart, and desiring with his whole heart to dwell ceaselessly with God, he gave himself over unto the utmost rigorous discipline. And drawing back his senses with watchful prudence on both sides and habituating them unto temperance, elevating his thought and intellect unto God, spending all his time in prayers and contemplation of God, and ordering his life in an exquisite manner, he utterly vanquished demonic assaults by divine aid; and having cleansed his soul through all-night standing by streams of tears, he became a chosen vessel of the gifts of the Divine Spirit (Acts 9:15), and beheld frequent and almost continual divine visions. And what is most marvelous: even when compelled by Ishmaelite incursions and raids to journey unto Thessalonica and to the Skete at Veroia,[^1238] and being constrained to converse with certain townsfolk, even so he did not turn aside from his wilderness discipline unto urban pastimes. Having, therefore, over no few years thoroughly purified both body and soul, by divine decree he received the great anointing of the priesthood; and being as it were immaterial, and so to speak, outside of himself, the mysteries of that...

Для то́го те́жъ и҆ має́тность ᲂу҆бѡ́гимъ по Є҆ѵ҃лїю̀ розда́вши, ща́стє и҆ добро́є мѣ́нє Ца́рское, и҆ че́сти, и҆ похва́лы в дома́хъ Кроле́вскихъ ве́село и҆ до́брымъ срⷵцемъ зоста́вивши, шо́лъ за хрⷭ҇томъ. Ма́тку те́ды и҆ Се́стры к Монастырꙋ̀ Дѣви́чымъ постанови́вши, Бра́тїю за́сь з собо́ю вза́вши, на Го́рꙋ сто́сти тезоимени́тꙋю встꙋпи́лъ. А҆́ле бра́тїи намовля́етъ а҆́бы въ дрꙋги́хъ Монастыре́хъ преме́шкова́ли, и҆ за несдаре́нємъ ча́сꙋ зєдноти́вшисѧ є҆де́нъ з дрꙋги́мъ, живо́тъ бг҃ꙋ пра́вова́дили, а҆ себѐ само́го в послꙋше́нство и҆ спра́вова́нє чꙋдо́вногѡ є҆дногѡ мꙋ́жа ве́длꙋгъ ти́хогѡ и҆ молчали́вогѡ живота̀, само́мꙋ кꙋ̀ живо́тꙋ тогѡ̀ ѡ҆дає́тъ, и҆́менемъ Никоди́мови: ѿ кото́рогѡ вшеля́когѡ приказа́нѧ бж҃ского, вшеля́кои цно́ты в поко́рности дꙋше́внои са́мымъ скꙋ́ткомъ навчи́вшисѧ, и҆ Всест҃о́и бц҃и застꙋпле́нїе и҆ ѡ҆боро́нꙋ къ всѣ̑мъ ре́чамъ незва́лченꙋю и҆ непрела́манꙋю въ ѡ҆бѧ́вленїи та́емномъ та́мъ принѧ́вши, по ѡ҆́ногѡ ꙗ҆́жъ до бг҃а ѿше́стїи. И҆ въ вели́кои Ла́ѵрѣ лѣ́тъ ко́лко переме́шкавши, з ба́рзо вели́кою ѡ҆хо́тою, и҆ дозрѣ́лымъ и҆ доскона́лымъ ро́зꙋмомъ, ми́лости ти́хогѡ и҆ молчали́вогѡ живота̀. ѿ Ла́ѵры выхо́дитъ, и҆ до пꙋсты́ни любо́вне встꙋпа́етъ, и҆ любо́въ бж҃їю за́вше до любвѝ приклада́ючи, и҆ в срⷵцꙋ свое́мъ помина́ючи, нє̀ бм҃ъ оу҆ста́вичне поспо́лꙋ жи́ти всѣ̑мъ срⷵцемъ пожада́ючи, на ѡ҆ста́тнєє сро́гоє цвиче́нє себѐ выдає́тъ. И҆ ѡ҆па́трности ѡ҆сторо́жнои з ѡ҆бѣ́хъ сторо́нъ змы́слы своє̀ повита́гнꙋвши, и҆ до скро́мности привѣ́кши, а҆ к бг҃ꙋ мы́сль свою̀ и҆ ро́зꙋмъ повы́шивъши, и҆ ча́съ весь на мл҃твахъ и҆ бг҃омы́слености заба́вивши, и҆ живо́тъ спорѧди́вши свои̑ превыбо́рне, бѣсо́вскїи ко́йны по́мочꙋ бж҃ею, до ща́дꙋ звытѧ́жаєтъ, и҆ всено́чнымъ стоѧ́ньемъ пре жро́дла сле́зъ дꙋшꙋ̀ ѡ҆чи́стивши, начи́нїемъ выбо́рнымъ да́рѡвъ бж҃твеннагѡ дх҃а зоста́лъ, и҆ бж҃скїи зъѧвле́нѧ ча́стыи, и҆ нема́лъ оу҆ста́вичныи вида́лъ. А҆ што̀ чꙋдовнѣ́йшаѧ, и҆́жъ и҆ прехоже́на пре неима́нїтїскїи навѣ̑ти и҆ вта́рчки, до Ѳессалони́ки, и҆ до Ски́тꙋ в Ве́ррїи бꙋдꙋчого ѿпра́вꙋючи, и҆ з нѣ́которыми мѣ́стами розмо́вꙋ мѣ́ти примꙋшаный бꙋ́дꙋчи, а҆ ни та́къ преходи́лъ з пꙋсты́нного своего̀ цвиче́нѧ сѧ, на мѣ́щскїи заба́вы. Пре лѣ́та те́ды нема́лыи доскона́ле и҆ тѣ́ло и҆ дꙋ́шꙋ ѡ҆чи́стивши, и҆ за бж҃скимъ вы́рокомъ, вели́кое пома́занє сщ҃енства принѧ́лъ, и҆ ꙗ҆́кѡ бы ꙗ҆́кїи нематерїа́лный, и҆ та́къ ре́кши, з надво́ра само́гѡ себѐ бꙋдꙋ́чїй, та́емницы тогѡ̀
units.english_text: This son of the divine and never-waning light, a true man of the true God, and a marvelous minister and worker of divine deeds, had in truth for his homeland the city reigning over all cities [Constantinople],[^1234] and noble and renowned parents, who endeavored to adorn him not merely outwardly and according to human carnal thinking, but far more inwardly and invisibly with virtue and learning. When, therefore, while he was yet in his very early years, his father passed away, his mother nurtured and reared him, as well as his brothers and sisters, in learning and in the Law of the Lord, as also in the Holy Scriptures, and knew how to value well him who acquired outward wisdom among teachers. And having united the keenness of his natural wit with diligence in learning, in a short time he mastered all logical learning. And when he was twenty years of age, regarding all earthly things as contemptible and ultimately deceitful, he sought to flee and turn unto God, the Cause and Giver of all wisdom, and through a more perfect life to offer himself entirely and wholly unto Him. Concerning this goal and purpose, he disclosed his very great delight and burning love toward God unto his God-loving mother, whom he found, although sorrowful, yet rejoicing together with him in this. Immediately, therefore, his mother assembled the children who were with her, and saying with joy: "Behold, the children whom God has given me!" (Isa. 8:18; Heb. 2:13), she tested their disposition toward goodness, and revealed unto them the great goal and undertaking. He also addressed exhortatory words unto them, and more swiftly than can be told, he won them all over, persuaded and instructed, fleeing with zeal from this life and going forth unto a like love toward God. Therefore, having also distributed his estate unto the poor according to the Gospel (Matt. 19:21; Luke 18:22), and having left with joy and a good heart earthly fortune, the imperial estate, honors, and praises in royal courts, he followed Christ. Having, therefore, placed his mother and sisters in a convent of virgins, and taking his brothers with him, he ascended the mount eponymous with sanctity [the Holy Mountain of Athos].[^1235] Yet he persuaded his brothers to dwell in other monasteries, that, being united one with another without untimely distractions, they might direct their lives toward God; while he himself submitted to the obedience and guidance of a marvelous man according to the quiet and hesychastic life, giving himself over unto that manner of life, to a father named Nicodemus;[^1236] from whom having learned every divine commandment and every virtue in spiritual humility by actual deed, and having received there in a mystical revelation the invincible and unyielding protection and defense of the All-Holy Mother of God in all things, he remained until the elder's departure unto God. And having dwelt several years in the Great Lavra [of St. Athanasius],[^1237] with very great eagerness and mature and perfected understanding, through love for the quiet and hesychastic life he departed from the Lavra and entered lovingly into the wilderness; and ever adding divine love unto love, remembering God in his heart, and desiring with his whole heart to dwell ceaselessly with God, he gave himself over unto the utmost rigorous discipline. And drawing back his senses with watchful prudence on both sides and habituating them unto temperance, elevating his thought and intellect unto God, spending all his time in prayers and contemplation of God, and ordering his life in an exquisite manner, he utterly vanquished demonic assaults by divine aid; and having cleansed his soul through all-night standing by streams of tears, he became a chosen vessel of the gifts of the Divine Spirit (Acts 9:15), and beheld frequent and almost continual divine visions. And what is most marvelous: even when compelled by Ishmaelite incursions and raids to journey unto Thessalonica and to the Skete at Veroia,[^1238] and being constrained to converse with certain townsfolk, even so he did not turn aside from his wilderness discipline unto urban pastimes. Having, therefore, over no few years thoroughly purified both body and soul, by divine decree he received the great anointing of the priesthood; and being as it were immaterial, and so to speak, outside of himself, the mysteries of that...

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: Се́й бж҃е́ственныѧ и҆ без̾вечернѧѧ и҆мѣ́ѧщеи свѣ́тлости Сы́нъ, правди́вый правди́вагѡ бг҃а чл҃къ, и҆ чꙋдо́вный бж҃скихъ спра́въ слꙋжи́тель и҆ дѣ́латель, ѿчи́знꙋ въ пра́вдѣ мѣ́лъ мѣ́сто надъ всѣ́ми мѣ́стами царство́ючее, а҆ роди́телєвъ за́цныхъ и҆ сла́вныхъ, кото́рїи є҆гѡ̀ не позвѣ́рхо́вне то́лко и҆ водлꙋ́гъ змы́слености члове́кои, а҆ле дале́кѡ ба́рзѣй внꙋ́трне и҆ неви́домымъ, цно́тою и҆ навꙋ́кою приѡздо́бити стара́лисѧ. Гды́ те́ды є҆мꙋ̀ ба́рзо молоды́хъ лѣ́техъ бꙋ́дꙋчемꙋ ѿте́цъ скончи́лсѧ, ма́тка та́къ є҆го̀ само́го, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆ бра́тїю є҆го̀ и҆ се́стры в навꙋ́цѣ и҆ Зако́нѣ гдⷭ҇немъ та́кже в сто́мъ пи́смѣ вы́кормила и҆ вы́ховала, и҆ того̀ кото́рый позвѣ́рховноѣ мꙋ́дрости межъ оу҆чи́телми навыка́лъ, до́брѣ цѣни́ти оу҆мѣ́ла. кото́рый ѡ҆стрости прирожо́ного довтѣ́пꙋ, пи́лност в навꙋ́цѣ взае́мне зєдночи́вши, в мало́мъ ча́сѣ всеѣ логї́ческоѣ навы́къ оу҆мѣ́етности. А҆ гды́ былъ въ два́дцати лѣ́техъ, всѣ́ собѣ̀ ре́чи на землѝ взга́ржоныи, и҆ на́ конъ ба́рзѣй ѡ҆шꙋкава́телными почитны́вши, шꙋка́лъ оу҆течи́сѧ и҆ оу҆да́ти до причи́нци и҆ пода́вцы все́й мꙋ́дрости бг҃а, и҆ пре́зъ живо́тъ доскона́лшїй, себѐ всего̀ ѻ҆́номꙋ ца́ло ѡ҆фѣрова́ти. units.slavonic_diplomatic: сщ҃енства выконыва́лъ, и҆́жъ мно́гїи ви́дѣли, ꙗ҆́къ смотрѧ́щихъ на не́гѡ до оу҆миле́нїѧ и҆ пла́чꙋ приводи́лъ дш҃и. Вели́кїй бы́лъ заи́сте, и҆ ты̑мъ которыи живо́тъ ве́длꙋгъ бг҃а, и҆ за дх҃оно́сца бы́лъ зна́ный. ѡ҆казова́лсѧ те́жъ таковы́мъ бꙋ́дꙋчи, и҆ з надво́рѧ на не́гѡ смотрѧ́чымъ, мо́цъ ма́ючы на бѣ́сы, и҆ ѿ и҆́хъ ѡ҆шꙋканѧ и҆ прохы́рства ѡ҆панова́ныхъ ѡ҆свобожа́ючи, непло́дность дере́въ въ ѡ҆кби́тость преклада́ючи, при́шлыи ре́чи в про́дъ ѡ҆бача́ючи, и҆ и҆́ными бж҃твеннагѡ дх҃а да́рами и҆ ѡ҆́вогцами бы́лъ приѡздо́бленый. И҆ то́е в пра́вдѣ жебы́смы в цно́тахъ працовалѝ: ве вла́дзы на́шой є҆́стъ поло́жено, а҆ в напа́сти и҆ покꙋ́сы впада́ти, не є҆́стъ оу҆ на́съ. Бе́з ты́хъ за́сь не мо́жетъ бы́ти доскона́лость, а҆́лбо ѡ҆каза́нє и҆ ѡ҆свѣ́дче́нє кꙋ бг҃ꙋ вѣ́ры. (Зше́дшиесѧ со́вѣмъ, мо́витъ, справо́ванє и҆ терпе́нє в добро́мъ, доскона́лымъ чи́нѧтъ ве́длꙋгъ бг҃а чл҃ка), попꙋща́етсѧ семꙋ̀ вели́комꙋ в розма́итыи и҆ оу҆ста́внуныи впада́ти покꙋ́сы, жебы́сѧ пре́ всѣ̑ ре́чи доскона́лый и҆сто́тне ѡ҆каза́. Ѿ тогѡ̀ за́сь ча́сꙋ, кото́рый ро́зꙋмъ помы́слити мо́жетъ; кото́рое выповѣ́сть сло́во, штꙋ́ки и҆ хи́трости напе́ршїи дале́ко бо́лшїи, ѡ҆крꙋ́тногѡ бое́вника; та́кже зелжи́вости и҆ потва́ри на не́гѡ нововзни́клыхъ бг҃обо́рцѡвъ, и҆́жъ мно́гїи за бл҃гчⷭ҇тїе, ко́йнув пре цѣ́лыи два́дцатъ и҆ трѝ лѣ́та ѿ ни́хъ оу҆терпѣ́лъ бѣ́ды и҆ оу҆трапе́ж вшелѧ́кїи. А҆бо́вемъ І҆талї́йскаѧ бе́стїа Калаврї́йскїй Варлаа́мъ, позвѣ́рховною мꙋ́дрости мно́гѡ мꙋ́дрꙋючи, и҆ ма́рно́стїю сво́й ро́зꙋмꙋ выне́слыхъ и҆ порожни́ мы́слей все вѣ́дати и҆ оу҆мѣ́ти мнѣма́ючи, сро́внꙋ подно́ситъ во́йнꙋ на Це́рковь хв҃ꙋ, и҆ на бл҃гчⷭ҇ти́вꙋю нашꙋ вѣ́рꙋ, и҆ на ты́хъ которы́и є҆и́ мо́цнѡ задержꙋ́ю: спо́лнꙋю бовѣ́мъ ла́скꙋ Ѻц҃а̀, и҆ Сн҃а, и҆ Дх҃а ст҃гѡ, и҆ свѣ́тлость при́шлогѡ вѣ́кꙋ которы́мъ и҆ справедли́вымъ сїѧ́ти бꙋ́дꙋтъ ꙗ҆́къ сл҃нце, ꙗ҆́къ и҆ хс҃ препоказа́лъ на горѣ̀ возсїѧ́вши, и҆ попро́стꙋ всю си́лꙋ и҆ є҆нергї́ю, то́ є҆стъ, спра́вꙋ Трїѷпоста́снагѡ бж҃ства, и҆ вшелѧ́кꙋю за́цность ꙗ҆ка́ѧ є҆но є҆́стъ бж҃скои натꙋ́ры, ство́ренꙋю бы́ти ро́зꙋмомъ свои́мъ зара́зливымъ мꙋ́дровалъ, и҆ навꙋча́лъ, и҆ ты́хъ которыи бл҃гчⷭ҇ти́вѡ мретво́нтъ нестворо́нꙋю бы́ти ѡ҆́нꙋю бж҃твеннѣ́йшꙋю свѣ́тлость, и҆ вшелѧ́кꙋю си́лꙋ и҆ спра́вованє, понева́жъ ничто́то не є҆́стъ нововзни́клое з ты рече́й которыи в бз҃ѣ̀ сꙋ́тъ натꙋра́лне, сло́вы и҆ пи́смы ѡ҆сши́рными дво́божными и҆менова́лъ, и҆ многѡбо́жными, ꙗ҆́къ жи́дове, Саве́лїй, и҆ А҆́рїй и҆менꙋ́етъ на́съ. Для то́гѡ те́ды бж҃твенный Григѡ́рїй, ꙗ҆́кѡ бл҃гчⷭ҇тїа поко́рникъ, и҆ предста́тель знамени́тый и҆ над̾ всѣ́хъ и҆ны́хъ, за то́е мо́влю, бл҃гчⷭ҇тїе и҆потыка́ючысѧ и҆ потва́рливе ѡ҆скаржо́ваный бꙋ́дꙋчи, посла́ный ѿ Цр҃кве Кѡнстантинопо́лскои, прихо́дитъ. Гды́ те́ды побо́жный и҆ сто́бливый Ца́ръ А҆ндро́никъ Бл҃гчⷭ҇тїа бы́лъ застꙋ́пцею, з Полеоло́гѡвъ четве́ртый, Собо́ръ ст҃ы́й згромажа́етсѧ. гдѣ̀ и҆ ѻ҆́ный Варлаа́м при́былъ, и҆ є҆гѡ̀ злочести́выи навки, и҆ на бл҃гчⷭ҇ти́вы помо́вника и҆ по́твары, Дх҃а ст҃гѡ напол́нившїисѧ вели́кїй Григѡ́рїй и҆ си́лою незавтажо́ною пришболо́кшисѧ збы́сокости, оу҆ста̀ свои ко́торыи былѝ ве́длꙋгъ бг҃а ѿтвори́вши, внѣ́ роздѣ́валси роспорошѝ, и҆ до конца̀ є҆го̀ завстыда́лъ, и҆ ѻ҆гнедꙋхнове́нными слова́ми и҆ пи́смомъ, хро́стꙋ подо́бныи є҆гѡ̀ є҆́реси в по́пелъ ѡ҆бернꙋ́лъ. Пре́то те́жъ со́ромꙋ знестѝ не могꙋ́чи бл҃гчⷭ҇тїа преслѣ́довца и҆ бое́вникъ, до Лати́нъ ѿко́ля пришо́лъ бы́лъ, оу҆тёкъ. А҆ по ѻ҆́номъ за́разъ А҆кинди́на, то́естъ, безбѣ́дного, а҆ ра́чей Поликїнді́на, то́естъ, многобѣ́дного сѷнода́лне пре всѣ́мъ Собо́ромъ строфꙋ́етъ, и҆ є҆гѡ̀ пи́сма, слова́ми проти́вными зно́ситъ и҆ распоро́шꙋетъ, ты́и є҆дна́къ которыи и҆́хъ зара́зы оу҆ча́стниками зоста́ли, а҆ни та́къ попереста́ли воєва́ти на Цр҃квъ бж҃їю. По́тымъ и҆ за мꙋ́ромъ вели́кимъ Сщ҃еннагѡ Собо́ра, а҆ наи́ве за само́гѡ Царѧ̀ сто́бливымъ вы́рокомъ приведе́ный и҆ намо́вленый Григѡ́рїй, на А҆рхїере́йскїй подно́ситсѧ Престо́лъ, и҆ Ѳессалони́цкои сто́и Цр҃кви Па́стыръ поставлѧ́етсѧ. Пре́то те́жъ дале́кѡ бо́лшїи напе́ршїи по́двиги и҆ пра́цы ѡ҆́коло вѣ́ры Правосла́внои прїи́мбетъ и҆ пока́зꙋетъ, а҆ то мꙋ́жески, стате́чне и҆ терпли́ве. Злосли́выхъ а҆́бовемъ сꙋкцессо́рѡвъ, то́естъ, настꙋпникѡвъ А҆кинді́новыхъ и҆ Варлаа́мовыхъ, которы́исѧ мно́гїи и҆ сро́гїи ѡ҆каза́ли, и҆ ѡ҆крꙋ́тныхъ и҆ ꙗ҆дови́тыхъ звѣ́рѡвъ ѡ҆крꙋ́тныи щенѧ́та, и҆́нхъ навки и҆ пи́сма, не ра́зъ, не два́кроть и҆ не три́кроть, а҆ле часто́кроть и҆ пре ча́съ долгїй, не за є҆дно́го Царѧ̀ а҆́лбѡ Патрїа́рха, а҆ле за тре́хъ є҆дны́хъ по є҆дны́хъ настꙋпꙋ́ючи, и҆ ски́птра Ца́рства прїимꙋ́ючи за то́лкожъ и҆ Патрїа́рхѡ́, и҆ пре Сѷнѡ́ды незали́чоныи, слова́ми и҆ пи́смы Бг҃одꙋхнове́нными, премно́гїи спо́собы, выворотѧ́етъ и҆ потлꙋмла́етъ, и҆ всѣ̑ми си́лами до грꙋ́нтꙋ зно́ситъ и҆ звѣтѧжа́етъ: хо́тьто нѣ́которыи з ни́хъ невмы́сннѡ въ оу҆по́рѣ свое́мъ трва́ючи, ни за́ што положи́вши бы́въ ре́ченый правди́вый є҆гѡ̀ сꙋ́дъ и҆ вы́рокъ, та́ зоста́ли. Всѣ́хъ бовѣ́мъ є҆ресе́й, сꙋ́тъ є҆ще ѡ҆ста́тки, которыи невестыдли́ве повстава́ютъ на ты ст҃ы́хъ, которыи и҆́хъ вы́вернꙋли и҆ потлꙋми́ли,
units.english_cohort_translation: ...priesthood did he celebrate, that many beheld how he brought the souls of those who looked upon him to compunction and tears. Great indeed was he, and known as a Spirit-bearer by those who lived according to God; and being such, he was manifested even to those who looked upon him from without, having power over demons, liberating those possessed by their deception and cunning, turning the barrenness of trees into fruitfulness, foreseeing future things, and being adorned with other gifts and fruits of the Divine Spirit. And that in truth we should labor in virtues: this is placed within our power; but falling into afflictions and temptations is not within our control. Yet without these, perfection cannot be attained, nor can proof and witness of faith toward God be shown forth. ("Activity and endurance in goodness coming together," it is said, "make a man perfect according to God.") Therefore was it permitted for this great man to fall into diverse and continual trials, that he might be shown forth essentially perfect above all things. From that time forth, what intellect can conceive, what word can tell the arts and subtle machinations, far greater than before, of the cruel adversary? As well as the insults and slander against him by newly-arisen God-fighters, such that for the sake of piety this soldier endured troubles and every kind of affliction from them for twenty-three full years![^1239] For the Italian beast, Barlaam of Calabria,[^1240] philosophizing much according to outward wisdom, and in the vanity of his intellect puffed up with empty conceits, imagining that he knew and understood all things, raised up fierce war against the Church of Christ, against our pious faith, and against those who hold fast unto it. For the common grace of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, and the light of the age to come wherewith the righteous shall shine as the sun (Matt. 13:43), even as Christ prefigured when He shone upon the mount [Tabor] (Matt. 17:1–8), and simply all power and energy—that is, the operation of the Tri-hypostatic Godhead and every excellence belonging to the divine nature—he sophistically asserted and taught with his infected reason to be created! And those who piously confess that most divine light and every power and operation to be uncreated—since nothing of those things which exist naturally in God is newly-arisen—he labeled in extensive writings as ditheists and polytheists, just as the Jews, Sabellius, and Arius label us![^1241] For this cause, therefore, the divine Gregory, as a champion of piety and an illustrious defender and above all others, for the sake of piety, I say, having contended and being slanderously accused, being summoned by the Church of Constantinople, he arrived. When, therefore, the pious and constant Emperor Andronicus IV [III] Palaeologus was champion of piety,[^1242] a Holy Council was assembled [Constantinople, 1341],[^1243] where that same Barlaam also arrived with his impious teachings, slander, and insults against the pious; but the great Gregory, being filled with the Holy Spirit and invested from on high with invincible power, opening his mouth which was according to God, utterly scattered and put him to shame unto the end, and by fire-breathing words and writings burned up his brushwood-like heresies into ashes! Therefore, unable to bear the shame, this persecutor and combatant against piety fled unto the Latins, whence he had come.[^1244] And immediately after him, Gregory synodically rebuked Akindynos—that is, "dangerless," or rather Polykindynos, that is, "of many dangers"[^1245]—before the entire Council, and overturned and scattered his writings with refuting words; yet those who became partakers of their contagion ceased not even then to wage war against the Church of God. Afterwards, through the great fortification of the Holy Council, and especially persuaded and directed by the firm judgment of the Emperor himself, Gregory was elevated to the Hierarchical Throne, and was established as Pastor of the holy Church of Thessalonica.[^1246] Therefore he took upon himself and showed forth even far greater struggles and labors for the Orthodox faith, and that valiantly, steadfastly, and patiently. For against the malicious successors, that is, the followers of Akindynos and Barlaam, who showed themselves numerous and harsh—cruel whelps of cruel and venomous beasts—he overturned and silenced their teachings and writings not once, nor twice, nor thrice, but frequently and over a long period, not under one Emperor or Patriarch, but under three successive Emperors holding the scepter of the Empire, and under as many Patriarchs,[^1247] and before innumerable Synods, by God-inspired words and writings, by manifold means, overthrowing and suppressing them, and with all his might utterly demolishing and conquering them; even though certain of them, persisting willfully in their stubbornness and counting for naught his aforesaid righteous judgment and sentence, remained in their error. For of all heresies there are yet remnants that shamelessly rise up against those saints who overthrew and suppressed them...
units.slavonic_text: сщ҃енства выконыва́лъ, и҆́жъ мно́гїи ви́дѣли, ꙗ҆́къ смотрѧ́щихъ на не́гѡ до оу҆миле́нїѧ и҆ пла́чꙋ приводи́лъ дш҃и. Вели́кїй бы́лъ заи́сте, и҆ ты̑мъ которыи живо́тъ ве́длꙋгъ бг҃а, и҆ за дх҃оно́сца бы́лъ зна́ный. ѡ҆казова́лсѧ те́жъ таковы́мъ бꙋ́дꙋчи, и҆ з надво́рѧ на не́гѡ смотрѧ́чымъ, мо́цъ ма́ючы на бѣ́сы, и҆ ѿ и҆́хъ ѡ҆шꙋканѧ и҆ прохы́рства ѡ҆панова́ныхъ ѡ҆свобожа́ючи, непло́дность дере́въ въ ѡ҆кби́тость преклада́ючи, при́шлыи ре́чи в про́дъ ѡ҆бача́ючи, и҆ и҆́ными бж҃твеннагѡ дх҃а да́рами и҆ ѡ҆́вогцами бы́лъ приѡздо́бленый. И҆ то́е в пра́вдѣ жебы́смы в цно́тахъ працовалѝ: ве вла́дзы на́шой є҆́стъ поло́жено, а҆ в напа́сти и҆ покꙋ́сы впада́ти, не є҆́стъ оу҆ на́съ. Бе́з ты́хъ за́сь не мо́жетъ бы́ти доскона́лость, а҆́лбо ѡ҆каза́нє и҆ ѡ҆свѣ́дче́нє кꙋ бг҃ꙋ вѣ́ры. Ѿ тогѡ̀ за́сь ча́сꙋ, кото́рый ро́зꙋмъ помы́слити мо́жетъ; кото́рое выповѣ́сть сло́во, штꙋ́ки и҆ хи́трости напе́ршїи дале́ко бо́лшїи, ѡ҆крꙋ́тногѡ бое́вника; та́кже зелжи́вости и҆ потва́ри на не́гѡ нововзни́клыхъ бг҃обо́рцѡвъ, и҆́жъ мно́гїи за бл҃гчⷭ҇тїе, ко́йнув пре цѣ́лыи два́дцатъ и҆ трѝ лѣ́та ѿ ни́хъ оу҆терпѣ́лъ бѣ́ды и҆ оу҆трапе́ж вшелѧ́кїи. Злосли́выхъ а҆́бовемъ сꙋкцессо́рѡвъ, то́естъ, настꙋпникѡвъ А҆кинді́новыхъ и҆ Варлаа́мовыхъ, которы́исѧ мно́гїи и҆ сро́гїи ѡ҆каза́ли, и҆ ѡ҆крꙋ́тныхъ и҆ ꙗ҆дови́тыхъ звѣ́рѡвъ ѡ҆крꙋ́тныи щенѧ́та, и҆́нхъ навки и҆ пи́сма, не ра́зъ, не два́кроть и҆ не три́кроть, а҆ле часто́кроть и҆ пре ча́съ долгїй, не за є҆дно́го Царѧ̀ а҆́лбѡ Патрїа́рха, а҆ле за тре́хъ є҆дны́хъ по є҆дны́хъ настꙋпꙋ́ючи, и҆ ски́птра Ца́рства прїимꙋ́ючи за то́лкожъ и҆ Патрїа́рхѡ́, и҆ пре Сѷнѡ́ды незали́чоныи, слова́ми и҆ пи́смы Бг҃одꙋхнове́нными, премно́гїи спо́собы, выворотѧ́етъ и҆ потлꙋмла́етъ, и҆ всѣ̑ми си́лами до грꙋ́нтꙋ зно́ситъ и҆ звѣтѧжа́етъ: хо́тьто нѣ́которыи з ни́хъ невмы́сннѡ въ оу҆по́рѣ свое́мъ трва́ючи, ни за́ што положи́вши бы́въ ре́ченый правди́вый є҆гѡ̀ сꙋ́дъ и҆ вы́рокъ, та́ зоста́ли. Всѣ́хъ бовѣ́мъ є҆ресе́й, сꙋ́тъ є҆ще ѡ҆ста́тки, которыи невестыдли́ве повстава́ютъ на ты ст҃ы́хъ, которыи и҆́хъ вы́вернꙋли и҆ потлꙋми́ли,
units.english_text: ...priesthood did he celebrate, that many beheld how he brought the souls of those who looked upon him to compunction and tears. Great indeed was he, and known as a Spirit-bearer by those who lived according to God; and being such, he was manifested even to those who looked upon him from without, having power over demons, liberating those possessed by their deception and cunning, turning the barrenness of trees into fruitfulness, foreseeing future things, and being adorned with other gifts and fruits of the Divine Spirit. And that in truth we should labor in virtues: this is placed within our power; but falling into afflictions and temptations is not within our control. Yet without these, perfection cannot be attained, nor can proof and witness of faith toward God be shown forth. ("Activity and endurance in goodness coming together," it is said, "make a man perfect according to God.") Therefore was it permitted for this great man to fall into diverse and continual trials, that he might be shown forth essentially perfect above all things. From that time forth, what intellect can conceive, what word can tell the arts and subtle machinations, far greater than before, of the cruel adversary? As well as the insults and slander against him by newly-arisen God-fighters, such that for the sake of piety this soldier endured troubles and every kind of affliction from them for twenty-three full years![^1239] For the Italian beast, Barlaam of Calabria,[^1240] philosophizing much according to outward wisdom, and in the vanity of his intellect puffed up with empty conceits, imagining that he knew and understood all things, raised up fierce war against the Church of Christ, against our pious faith, and against those who hold fast unto it. For the common grace of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, and the light of the age to come wherewith the righteous shall shine as the sun (Matt. 13:43), even as Christ prefigured when He shone upon the mount [Tabor] (Matt. 17:1–8), and simply all power and energy—that is, the operation of the Tri-hypostatic Godhead and every excellence belonging to the divine nature—he sophistically asserted and taught with his infected reason to be created! And those who piously confess that most divine light and every power and operation to be uncreated—since nothing of those things which exist naturally in God is newly-arisen—he labeled in extensive writings as ditheists and polytheists, just as the Jews, Sabellius, and Arius label us![^1241] For this cause, therefore, the divine Gregory, as a champion of piety and an illustrious defender and above all others, for the sake of piety, I say, having contended and being slanderously accused, being summoned by the Church of Constantinople, he arrived. When, therefore, the pious and constant Emperor Andronicus IV [III] Palaeologus was champion of piety,[^1242] a Holy Council was assembled [Constantinople, 1341],[^1243] where that same Barlaam also arrived with his impious teachings, slander, and insults against the pious; but the great Gregory, being filled with the Holy Spirit and invested from on high with invincible power, opening his mouth which was according to God, utterly scattered and put him to shame unto the end, and by fire-breathing words and writings burned up his brushwood-like heresies into ashes! Therefore, unable to bear the shame, this persecutor and combatant against piety fled unto the Latins, whence he had come.[^1244] And immediately after him, Gregory synodically rebuked Akindynos—that is, "dangerless," or rather Polykindynos, that is, "of many dangers"[^1245]—before the entire Council, and overturned and scattered his writings with refuting words; yet those who became partakers of their contagion ceased not even then to wage war against the Church of God. Afterwards, through the great fortification of the Holy Council, and especially persuaded and directed by the firm judgment of the Emperor himself, Gregory was elevated to the Hierarchical Throne, and was established as Pastor of the holy Church of Thessalonica.[^1246] Therefore he took upon himself and showed forth even far greater struggles and labors for the Orthodox faith, and that valiantly, steadfastly, and patiently. For against the malicious successors, that is, the followers of Akindynos and Barlaam, who showed themselves numerous and harsh—cruel whelps of cruel and venomous beasts—he overturned and silenced their teachings and writings not once, nor twice, nor thrice, but frequently and over a long period, not under one Emperor or Patriarch, but under three successive Emperors holding the scepter of the Empire, and under as many Patriarchs,[^1247] and before innumerable Synods, by God-inspired words and writings, by manifold means, overthrowing and suppressing them, and with all his might utterly demolishing and conquering them; even though certain of them, persisting willfully in their stubbornness and counting for naught his aforesaid righteous judgment and sentence, remained in their error. For of all heresies there are yet remnants that shamelessly rise up against those saints who overthrew and suppressed them...

units.slavonic_diplomatic: а҆ неркꙋ́чи и҆ Жидо́вскїй вседе́рзый ро́жай, ꙗ҆́жъ и҆ до нинѣ́шнегѡ ча́сꙋ ꙗ҆́дъ ма́єтъ и҆ запали́твость шале́нꙋю на Хрⷭ҇та̀, кото́рогѡ замордова́лъ. То́лкїи те́ды и҆ та́къ вели́кїи а҆́ле вко́ротце моглы́сѧ вырази́ти вели́когѡ тогѡ̀ ст҃гѡ звѣтѧ́зства и҆ трїꙋ́мфы. Бг҃ъ за́сь спосо́бами невыповѣ́димыми, и҆ на Восхо́дъ тогѡ̀ посыла́етъ оу҆ч҃тлѧ. Вы́правленъ те́ды быва́етъ ꙗ҆́къ ста́рецъ чⷭ҇тный ѿ Ѳессалони́ки до Кѡнстантинопо́лѧ, гды́ напремѣ́нꙋ розма́итыи настопова́ли Ца́реве. Быва́етъ за́сь пои́маный ѿ А҆гари́нѡвъ, и҆ держа́ный пре цѣ́лый ро́къ, на мѣ́сца з мѣ́сцъ, и҆ з мѣ́стъ до мѣ́стъ перехо́дѧчи, и҆ оу҆чѧчи в стра́хꙋ всѣ́хъ Хв҃а Є҆ѵ҃лїа. и҆ тве́рдыхъ и҆ стате́чныхъ в пра́вдѣ змоцнѧ́ючи ба́рзѣй и҆ напомина́ючи в вѣ́рѣ трва́лыми бы́ти, а҆ в не́й хвѣ́ючыхсѧ попира́ючи, и҆ нѣ́которыи вонтпли́вости, и҆ пыта́нѧ ѡ҆ то́й ре́чи преклада́ныи, Бг҃омꙋ́дрнѡ розва́зꙋючи, ꙗ҆́ко зго́ла оу҆се́рдꙋванє в спра́вахъ которы́и припомина́лемъ наидостати́чнѣйшее ѿдава́лъ. З и҆ны́ми те́жъ невѣ́рными, и҆ не́ндзне ѡ҆дорба́ными хрⷭ҇тїанами, и҆ прилꙋчи́вшими сѧ до ѡ҆́ныхъ, и҆ роздира́ющими на́ше Вызна́нє ѡ҆ смотре́нїи втѣ́лѣ Гдⷭ҇а и҆ Бг҃а на́шегѡ, и҆ ѡ҆ Крⷭ҇тѣ̀ Чⷭ҇тно́мъ, и҆ ѡ҆ чти го́дныхъ ѡ҆́бразехъ, и҆ ѡ҆ поклоне́нїи и҆́мъ, кото́роє є҆́стъ оу҆ на́съ, часто́кроть вели́кимъ безпече́нствомъ розмовлѧ́лъ и҆ диепꙋтова́лъ. Ктомꙋ̀ и҆ ѡ҆ Мѡаме́дѣ, и҆ ѡ҆ мнѡ́гихъ и҆ны́хъ пыта́нѧхъ ѡ҆ ни́хъ преклада́ныхъ пото́жне и҆ пре розсꙋжа́ючи, є҆́дныхъ мѣ́лъ которы́исѧ є҆мꙋ̀ дивова́ли, а҆ дрꙋ́гихъ которы́и шале́нства зажива́ли и҆ рꙋ́ки подноси́ли, которы́и и҆ до конца̀ живота̀ Мꙋ́чнїкый ѡ҆вы́тлемъ привели́ бы є҆гѡ̀, гды́бы за бж҃скимъ про́мысломъ, надѣ́ею є҆гѡ̀ має́тностїи оу҆веденїи бꙋ́дꙋчи, оу҆ мы́слях не фолгова́ли. Што́ гды́сѧ ста́ло, ѿ Хрⷭ҇толю́бивыхъ быва́етъ вы́зволеный вели́кїй, и҆ до своего̀ ста́да Мꙋ́чнкъ бе́зкровный свѣ́тлѡ зно́вꙋ схо́дитъ, є҆дна́къ при и҆ны́хъ мно́ги и҆ вели́кихъ которы́й мѣ́лъ да́рахъ и҆ знамени́тыхъ спра́вахъ ѿ Хрⷭ҇та да́ныхъ, бы́лъ те́жъ приѡздо́бленый, и҆ ꙗ҆́звы ве́длꙋгъ Па́ѵла ма́ючи в собѣ̀ ѡ҆ста́тки. А҆ жебы́смы и҆ ѡ҆но́го которы́й є҆гѡ̀ назна́чнѣлъ показа́ли, то́е мѣ́лъ то́тъ ст҃ы́й в собѣ̀ наивла́снѣйшее, же бы́лъ насквы́тъ ти́хїй, скро́мный, и҆ поко́рный, є҆дна́къ не стороны̀ Бг҃а и҆ Бо́зскихъ спра́въ мо́ва, в ты́хъ бовѣ́мъ и҆ ба́рзо бы́лъ побо́рникъ вели́кїй, не па́матозло́бный назвы́тъ, и҆ не ма́ючїй зло́сти, стара́ючисѧ ве́длꙋгъ си́лы добротли́вости вето́вати ты̑мъ которыи кꙋ немꙋ̀ чи́мъко́лвекъ, ѡ҆каза́лисѧ злы́ми.
units.english_cohort_translation: ...not to mention the all-audacious Jewish race, which even unto the present time has venom and mad fury against Christ, Whom they murdered. So many and so great, though in brief, could the victories and triumphs of this great saint be expressed! God, moreover, by ineffable means, sent him as a teacher also unto the East. For as a venerable elder he was dispatched from Thessalonica unto Constantinople, when diverse Emperors succeeded one another. But he was taken captive by the Hagarenes [Ottoman Turks],[^1248] and detained for a whole year, passing from place to place and from city to city, teaching all in the fear of Christ's Gospel; strengthening even more those who were firm and steadfast in the truth, admonishing them to abide in the faith, supporting those wavering in it, and God-wisely resolving certain doubts and questions presented concerning this matter, so that in all things he rendered the most sufficient zeal in the deeds which I have recalled. With other infidels also, and wretchedly apostate Christians who had joined them, tearing asunder our Confession concerning the dispensation in the flesh of our Lord and God, concerning the Precious Cross, and concerning the honorable icons and the veneration given unto them which we practice, he conversed and disputed frequently with great boldness.[^1249] Furthermore, concerning Mohammed, and concerning many other questions presented by them, judging powerfully and thoroughly, he had some who marveled at him, while others exhibited fury and lifted up their hands, who would even have brought his life to an end by the crown of martyrdom, had they not, by divine Providence, being enticed by the hope of ransom for him, restrained their intentions. When this took place, this great man was ransomed by Christ-lovers, and as an unbloody martyr he returned luminously again unto his flock; yet among the many other great gifts and illustrious deeds given him by Christ, he was also adorned, bearing in himself, according to Paul, the remnants of the marks of Christ (Gal. 6:17). And that we may also show forth what characterized him most distinctly: this saint possessed this as his most proper trait, that he was exceedingly meek, modest, and humble—unless the discourse concerned God and divine matters, for in those he was a very great champion—never bearing a grudge, possessing no malice, striving according to the power of his goodness to requite with kindness those who in any way showed themselves evil toward him in no wise easily believing whatever someone said against another, being patient and magnanimous in every hardship of tribulations, standing superior to every luxury and vain glory, ever practicing poverty, simplicity, and frugality in all bodily necessities, and possessing steadfastness in patience through a very long time, with modesty, meekness, and joy, he ascended to such a summit of virtue that even to outsiders looking upon him it was evident and clear, and in the knowledge of all there remained veneration and wonder. His eyes were never empty of tears, but were filled with great sorrow through wellsprings of tears. Having thus from beginning unto end armed himself in fasting and waged war against passions and demons, having driven heretics far away from the Church of Christ, having expounded the Orthodox Faith by mouth and through writing, and having by these sealed all God-inspired Scripture, his life and words became as it were a kind of completion and seal of the life and words of the saints! Thereafter, having pastured his flock for about thirteen years in an apostolic and God-pleasing manner, and having directed it unto the heavenly sheepfold,[^1250] and simply speaking, having become a common benefactor of all Christians living at that time and thereafter, he was translated unto the transcendent life, having lived in all sixty-three years of age; and he gave over his spirit into the hands of God (Luke 23:46), and left his body unto his flock, which even at his departure shone radiantly and was glorified, as a kind of heritage and precious treasure. For by miracles it shows forth beneficence unto those approaching from every quarter, and grants the driving away of all diseases, whereof the history written concerning him relates not a few.[^1251] By the prayers, therefore, of that holy Gregory, O God, have mercy upon us, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

Быва́етъ за́сь пои́маный ѿ А҆гари́нѡвъ, и҆ держа́ный пре цѣ́лый ро́къ, на мѣ́сца з мѣ́сцъ, и҆ з мѣ́стъ до мѣ́стъ перехо́дѧчи, и҆ оу҆чѧчи в стра́хꙋ всѣ́хъ Хв҃а Є҆ѵ҃лїа. и҆ тве́рдыхъ и҆ стате́чныхъ в пра́вдѣ змоцнѧ́ючи ба́рзѣй и҆ напомина́ючи в вѣ́рѣ трва́лыми бы́ти, а҆ в не́й хвѣ́ючыхсѧ попира́ючи, и҆ нѣ́которыи вонтпли́вости, и҆ пыта́нѧ ѡ҆ то́й ре́чи преклада́ныи, Бг҃омꙋ́дрнѡ розва́зꙋючи, ꙗ҆́ко зго́ла оу҆се́рдꙋванє в спра́вахъ которы́и припомина́лемъ наидостати́чнѣйшее ѿдава́лъ. З и҆ны́ми те́жъ невѣ́рными, и҆ не́ндзне ѡ҆дорба́ными хрⷭ҇тїанами, и҆ прилꙋчи́вшими сѧ до ѡ҆́ныхъ, и҆ роздира́ющими на́ше Вызна́нє ѡ҆ смотре́нїи втѣ́лѣ Гдⷭ҇а и҆ Бг҃а на́шегѡ, и҆ ѡ҆ Крⷭ҇тѣ̀ Чⷭ҇тно́мъ, и҆ ѡ҆ чти го́дныхъ ѡ҆́бразехъ, и҆ ѡ҆ поклоне́нїи и҆́мъ, кото́роє є҆́стъ оу҆ на́съ, часто́кроть вели́кимъ безпече́нствомъ розмовлѧ́лъ и҆ диепꙋтова́лъ. Ктомꙋ̀ и҆ ѡ҆ Мѡаме́дѣ, и҆ ѡ҆ мнѡ́гихъ и҆ны́хъ пыта́нѧхъ ѡ҆ ни́хъ преклада́ныхъ пото́жне и҆ пре розсꙋжа́ючи, є҆́дныхъ мѣ́лъ которы́исѧ є҆мꙋ̀ дивова́ли, а҆ дрꙋ́гихъ которы́и шале́нства зажива́ли и҆ рꙋ́ки подноси́ли, которы́и и҆ до конца̀ живота̀ Мꙋ́чнїкый ѡ҆вы́тлемъ привели́ бы є҆гѡ̀, гды́бы за бж҃скимъ про́мысломъ, надѣ́ею є҆гѡ̀ має́тностїи оу҆веденїи бꙋ́дꙋчи, оу҆ мы́слях не фолгова́ли. Што́ гды́сѧ ста́ло, ѿ Хрⷭ҇толю́бивыхъ быва́етъ вы́зволеный вели́кїй, и҆ до своего̀ ста́да Мꙋ́чнкъ бе́зкровный свѣ́тлѡ зно́вꙋ схо́дитъ, є҆дна́къ при и҆ны́хъ мно́ги и҆ вели́кихъ которы́й мѣ́лъ да́рахъ и҆ знамени́тыхъ спра́вахъ ѿ Хрⷭ҇та да́ныхъ, бы́лъ те́жъ приѡздо́бленый, и҆ ꙗ҆́звы ве́длꙋгъ Па́ѵла ма́ючи в собѣ̀ ѡ҆ста́тки. А҆ жебы́смы и҆ ѡ҆но́го которы́й є҆гѡ̀ назна́чнѣлъ показа́ли, то́е мѣ́лъ то́тъ ст҃ы́й в собѣ̀ наивла́снѣйшее, же бы́лъ насквы́тъ ти́хїй, скро́мный, и҆ поко́рный, є҆дна́къ не стороны̀ Бг҃а и҆ Бо́зскихъ спра́въ мо́ва, в ты́хъ бовѣ́мъ и҆ ба́рзо бы́лъ побо́рникъ вели́кїй, не па́матозло́бный назвы́тъ, и҆ не ма́ючїй зло́сти, стара́ючисѧ ве́длꙋгъ си́лы добротли́вости вето́вати ты̑мъ которыи кꙋ немꙋ̀ чи́мъко́лвекъ, ѡ҆каза́лисѧ злы́ми.
units.english_text: ...not to mention the all-audacious Jewish race, which even unto the present time has venom and mad fury against Christ, Whom they murdered. So many and so great, though in brief, could the victories and triumphs of this great saint be expressed! God, moreover, by ineffable means, sent him as a teacher also unto the East. For as a venerable elder he was dispatched from Thessalonica unto Constantinople, when diverse Emperors succeeded one another. But he was taken captive by the Hagarenes [Ottoman Turks],[^1248] and detained for a whole year, passing from place to place and from city to city, teaching all in the fear of Christ's Gospel; strengthening even more those who were firm and steadfast in the truth, admonishing them to abide in the faith, supporting those wavering in it, and God-wisely resolving certain doubts and questions presented concerning this matter, so that in all things he rendered the most sufficient zeal in the deeds which I have recalled. With other infidels also, and wretchedly apostate Christians who had joined them, tearing asunder our Confession concerning the dispensation in the flesh of our Lord and God, concerning the Precious Cross, and concerning the honorable icons and the veneration given unto them which we practice, he conversed and disputed frequently with great boldness.[^1249] Furthermore, concerning Mohammed, and concerning many other questions presented by them, judging powerfully and thoroughly, he had some who marveled at him, while others exhibited fury and lifted up their hands, who would even have brought his life to an end by the crown of martyrdom, had they not, by divine Providence, being enticed by the hope of ransom for him, restrained their intentions. When this took place, this great man was ransomed by Christ-lovers, and as an unbloody martyr he returned luminously again unto his flock; yet among the many other great gifts and illustrious deeds given him by Christ, he was also adorned, bearing in himself, according to Paul, the remnants of the marks of Christ (Gal. 6:17). And that we may also show forth what characterized him most distinctly: this saint possessed this as his most proper trait, that he was exceedingly meek, modest, and humble—unless the discourse concerned God and divine matters, for in those he was a very great champion—never bearing a grudge, possessing no malice, striving according to the power of his goodness to requite with kindness those who in any way showed themselves evil toward him in no wise easily believing whatever someone said against another, being patient and magnanimous in every hardship of tribulations, standing superior to every luxury and vain glory, ever practicing poverty, simplicity, and frugality in all bodily necessities, and possessing steadfastness in patience through a very long time, with modesty, meekness, and joy, he ascended to such a summit of virtue that even to outsiders looking upon him it was evident and clear, and in the knowledge of all there remained veneration and wonder. His eyes were never empty of tears, but were filled with great sorrow through wellsprings of tears. Having thus from beginning unto end armed himself in fasting and waged war against passions and demons, having driven heretics far away from the Church of Christ, having expounded the Orthodox Faith by mouth and through writing, and having by these sealed all God-inspired Scripture, his life and words became as it were a kind of completion and seal of the life and words of the saints! Thereafter, having pastured his flock for about thirteen years in an apostolic and God-pleasing manner, and having directed it unto the heavenly sheepfold,[^1250] and simply speaking, having become a common benefactor of all Christians living at that time and thereafter, he was translated unto the transcendent life, having lived in all sixty-three years of age; and he gave over his spirit into the hands of God (Luke 23:46), and left his body unto his flock, which even at his departure shone radiantly and was glorified, as a kind of heritage and precious treasure. For by miracles it shows forth beneficence unto those approaching from every quarter, and grants the driving away of all diseases, whereof the history written concerning him relates not a few.[^1251] By the prayers, therefore, of that holy Gregory, O God, have mercy upon us, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Тропа́рь:* Жесто́къ граждани́нъ, є҆мꙋ́же работа́ти ѡ҆кла́нный ѡ҆сꙋди́хсѧ, гла́дъ же, є҆го́же под̾ѧ́хъ, свинїѧ́мъ оу҆гожда́ѧ, крѣ́покъ и҆ нестерпи́мъ. но ѡ҆бра́щьсѧ прошꙋ̀, Сп҃се поми́лꙋй мѧ̀:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* Harsh is the citizen unto whom I, wretched one, was condemned to be in servitude; and the famine which I endured, tending swine, was grievous and intolerable (Luke 15:14–15); but having turned back, I pray: O Savior, have mercy upon me!

units.slavonic_incipit: Оу҆мерщве́нное є҆ст҃во̀ ѡ҆живи́ла є҆сѝ, є҆ди́на живо́тъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: оумерщвенное ество оживила еси едина живот рождшая дево
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Бг҃оро́диченъ:* Оу҆мерщве́нное є҆ст҃во̀ ѡ҆живи́ла є҆сѝ, є҆ди́на живо́тъ ро́ждшаѧ Дѣ́во Бц҃е. тѣ́мже тѧ̀ сп҃сенїе вѣ́рнїи свѣ́мы, ѻ҆тє́цъ на́шихъ Бг҃а пло́тїю ро́ждшꙋю:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Theotokion:* Thou didst vivify our deadened nature, O Virgin Mother of God, who alone didst bear Life; therefore, we, the faithful, know thee to be salvation, who didst bear in the flesh the God of our fathers!

units.slavonic_incipit: Словесе́мъ бесѣ́дꙋющїи, и҆ писа́нїемъ твои̑мъ Григѡ́рїе,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: словесем беседующии и писанием твоим григорие разум познавают
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Тропа́рь:* Словесе́мъ бесѣ́дꙋющїи, и҆ писа́нїемъ твои̑мъ Григѡ́рїе, ра́зꙋмъ познава́ютъ Бж҃їй, и҆ по́лны ꙗ҆влѧ́ютсѧ премꙋ́дрости Бж҃їѧ дх҃овныѧ, и҆ несозда́ннꙋю бл҃гть и҆ дѣ́йство Бж҃їе Бг҃ослове́ствꙋютъ:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* They that converse with thy words and thy writings, O Gregory, come to know the mind of God; they are shown forth full of the spiritual wisdom of God, and they theologically proclaim the uncreated grace and energy of God![^1252]
units.slavonic_text: *Тропа́рь:* Словесе́мъ бесѣ́дꙋющїи, и҆ писа́нїемъ твои̑мъ Григѡ́рїе, ра́зꙋмъ познава́ютъ Бж҃їй, и҆ по́лны ꙗ҆влѧ́ютсѧ премꙋ́дрости Бж҃їѧ дх҃овныѧ, и҆ несозда́ннꙋю бл҃гть и҆ дѣ́йство Бж҃їе Бг҃ослове́ствꙋютъ:
units.english_text: *Troparion:* They that converse with thy words and thy writings, O Gregory, come to know the mind of God; they are shown forth full of the spiritual wisdom of God, and they theologically proclaim the uncreated grace and energy of God![^1252]

units.slavonic_incipit: Ме́чъ и҆ стрѣ́лы злосла́вныхъ сокрꙋши́лъ є҆сѝ,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: меч и стрелы злославных сокрушил еси и гордост
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Тропа́рь:* Ме́чъ и҆ стрѣ́лы злосла́вныхъ сокрꙋши́лъ є҆сѝ, и҆ го́рдость Варлаа́мовꙋ, и҆ всѧ́кꙋю си́лꙋ є҆рети́ческꙋю, ꙗ҆́кѡ досто́йнѡ расточи́лъ є҆сѝ, ꙗ҆́кѡ ка́мень превели́кїй пꙋчи́нꙋ І҆ера́рхо:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* Thou didst shatter the sword and arrows of the ill-believing, and the arrogance of Barlaam, and didst worthily scatter all heretical power, O Hierarch, like an immense stone cast into the abyss!

units.english_text: *Troparion:* Thou didst shatter the sword and arrows of the ill-believing, and the arrogance of Barlaam, and didst worthily scatter all heretical power, O Hierarch, like an immense stone cast into the abyss!

units.slavonic_incipit: Запечатлѣ́сѧ твои́ми словесы̀ и҆ догма́ты вѣ́ра
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: запечатлеся твоими словесы и догматы вера блгчтивых и
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Тропа́рь:* Запечатлѣ́сѧ твои́ми словесы̀ и҆ догма́ты вѣ́ра бл҃гчⷭ҇ти́выхъ, и҆ ꙗ҆́рость є҆ресе́й ѿгна̀ Григѡ́рїе, и҆ низложе́нїе правосла́вїѧ преста̀, и҆ крѣ́пость злосла́вныхъ:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* By thy words and dogmas the faith of the pious has been sealed, and the fury of heresies driven away, O Gregory; and the subversion of Orthodoxy and the strength of the ill-believing have ceased!

units.slavonic_incipit: Стрꙋ́ѧ тѧ̀ и҆сто́чника, оу҆схꙋ́шїи страстї́й болѣ́зньми
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: струя тя источника оусхушии страстий болезньми ведуще воистинну
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Бг҃оро́диченъ:* Стрꙋ́ѧ тѧ̀ и҆сто́чника, оу҆схꙋ́шїи страстї́й болѣ́зньми вѣ́дꙋще вои́стиннꙋ почерпа́емъ Сп҃сенїе, и҆ Бж҃твенныѧ стрꙋ́ѧ, и҆ вопїе́мъ, бл҃гослове́нъ всечⷭ҇таѧ пло́дъ твое́гѡ чре́ва:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Theotokion:* Knowing thee truly to be a stream and fountain, we who are dried up by the diseases of passions draw forth salvation and divine streams, and cry out: Blessed, O all-immaculate one, is the fruit of thy womb! (Luke 1:42).

units.slavonic_incipit: Седмь седмнце́ю пе́щь: *Тропа́рь:* Безмѣ́рнагѡ Влⷣко,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: седм седмнцею пещ тропар безмернаго влко и многаго
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Пѣ́снь, и҆: И҆рмо́съ:* Седмь седмнце́ю пе́щь: *Тропа́рь:* Безмѣ́рнагѡ Влⷣко, и҆ мно́гагѡ млⷵрдїѧ твое́гѡ свѣ́мы бога́тство, в тѧ̀ вѣ́ровавшїи. тѣ́мже ти припа́даемъ, со блꙋ́днымъ внїи те́плѣ, прїимѝ съгрѣши́вшыѧ, и҆ к тебѣ̀ прибѣ́гшыѧ. нѣ́сть бо нѣ́стъ грѣ́хъ ще́дре, ко́е чл҃колю́бїе побѣди́ти могі́й:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Tone 6. Ode 8. Heirmos:* The furnace was once kindled sevenfold for the godly ones; but bedewed by the Spirit, they cried out: All ye works of the Lord, bless ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* Having believed in Thee, O Master, we know the wealth of Thine unmeasured and abundant tenderheartedness; therefore, we fall down before Thee, crying warmly with the prodigal: Receive us who have sinned and fled unto Thee; for there is not, yea, there is no sin, O Merciful One, that is able to overcome Thy love for mankind!

units.slavonic_incipit: Млⷵрдїѧ ра́ди Влⷣко себѐ смири́въ, па́дшымъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: млрдия ради влко себе смирив падшым твоим сыновом
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Тропа́рь:* Млⷵрдїѧ ра́ди Влⷣко себѐ смири́въ, па́дшымъ твои̑мъ сыновѡ́мъ прибли́жилсѧ є҆сѝ. Са́мъ бо чл҃колю́бче срѣ́лъ є҆сѝ па́дшихъ, и҆ ѡ҆блобыза́еши, и҆ сп҃сенїе да́рꙋеши, а҆́ще и҆ кто̀ до́лꙋ паде́тъ, млⷭ҇ти́въ сы́й не гнѣ́ва́ешисѧ, ꙗ҆́кѡ чл҃колю́бецъ:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* For the sake of tender mercy humbling Thyself, O Master, Thou didst draw near unto Thy fallen sons; for Thou Thyself, O Lover of mankind, didst meet the fallen, and dost embrace them and grant salvation (Luke 15:20); even if one has fallen low, being merciful Thou art not angered, as Lover of mankind!

units.slavonic_incipit: Страшнѣ́йшїй сꙋ́дъ менѐ оу҆страша́етъ сѧ Влⷣко,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: страшнейший суд мене оустрашает ся влко ко тя
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Тропа́рь:* Страшнѣ́йшїй сꙋ́дъ менѐ оу҆страша́етъ сѧ Влⷣко, ꙗ҆́кѡ тѧ̀ чл҃колю́бца и҆ неѕло́бива зрѧ̀, не притѣка́ю к тебѣ̀, блꙋ́днагѡ зовы́й гла́сомъ, но въ лѣ́ности житїѐ препровожда́ю. ты̀ оу҆́бѡ млⷭ҇тивъ бꙋ́ди мнѣ̀, и҆ ѡ҆сꙋжде́нїѧ ѡ҆́ного и҆схитѝ ще́дре, покаѧ́нїѧ ра́ди:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* The most dreadful judgment terrifies me, O Master, for seeing Thee to be the Lover of mankind and without malice, I run not unto Thee, calling with the voice of the prodigal, but spend my life in slothfulness; be Thou, therefore, merciful unto me, and snatch me from that condemnation, O Merciful One, for the sake of repentance!

units.slavonic_incipit: *Тро́иченъ:* Не трѝ Бо́ги сла́вимъ, но
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: троичен не три боги славим но едино бжтво
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Тро́иченъ:* Не трѝ Бо́ги сла́вимъ, но є҆ди́но Бж҃тво̀, трѝ же вои́стиннꙋ соста́вы чтемъ. Ѻ҆ц҃а̀ нерожде́нна, и҆ рожде́нна Сн҃а ѿ Ѻ҆ц҃а̀, и҆ и҆схо́дна ѿ Ѻ҆ц҃а ст҃гѡ Дх҃а, Бг҃а є҆ди́наго трѡ́и, а҆́ще и҆ зва́нїе ко́еждѡ, ꙗ҆́кѡже Бг҃ъ є҆́сть вѣ́рнѡ сла́вимаѧ:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Triadikon:* We glorify not three Gods, but one Godhead; yet we truly honor three Hypostases: the unbegotten Father, and the Son begotten of the Father, and the Holy Spirit proceeding from the Father; one God in Trinity, even though each name is faithfully glorified as God!

units.slavonic_incipit: Ѿ мно́гихъ мѧ̀ всенепоро́чнаѧ напа́стїй преклоне́на,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: от многих мя всенепорочная напастий преклонена и печалий
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Бг҃оро́диченъ:* Ѿ мно́гихъ мѧ̀ всенепоро́чнаѧ напа́стїй преклоне́на, и҆ печа́лїй бꙋ́рею потоплѧ́ема, приста́нище Сп҃сенїѧ, твое́ю мл҃твою прⷱ҇таѧ и҆зба́ви, и҆ ѿ всѣ́хъ и҆схити́вши сп҃сѝ, да тѧ̀ досто́йнѡ ꙗ҆́кѡ те́плꙋю предста́телницꙋ, сла́влю Бц҃ꙋ въ всѧ̑ вѣ́ки:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Theotokion:* Bowed down by many afflictions, O all-immaculate one, and drowned by the tempest of griefs, deliver me by thy prayer, O most pure haven of salvation, and snatching me from all evils save me, that I may worthily glorify thee as a fervent defender, O Mother of God, unto all ages!

units.slavonic_incipit: Преста́лъ є҆сѝ нн҃ѣ Бг҃осло́вѡмъ, прⷭ҇толꙋ̀ всеще́драгѡ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: престал еси нне бгословом пртолу всещедраго ко подобный
units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Тропа́рь:* Преста́лъ є҆сѝ нн҃ѣ Бг҃осло́вѡмъ, прⷭ҇толꙋ̀ всеще́драгѡ ꙗ҆́кѡ подо́бный, си̑мъ и҆ є҆динонра́вный всемꙋ́дре Григѡ́рїе, Ѳессало́никїй предсѣда́телю, І҆ера́рхѡвъ добро́то, свѣ́тло оу҆краси́всѧ сла́вою Сщ҃еннонача́лїа, Бг҃ꙋ и҆ нн҃ѣ слꙋжа̀:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* Thou hast now joined the Theologians before the throne of the All-Merciful, as like unto them and of one character, O all-wise Gregory, primate of Thessalonica, beauty of Hierarchs, radiantly adorned with the glory of the sacred hierarchy, now ministering unto God!

units.slavonic_incipit: Вѣ́дый твоегѡ̀ чⷭ҇тое помышле́нїѧ Бг҃ъ, и҆
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: ведый твоего чтое помышления бг и прежде чрева
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Вѣ́дый твоегѡ̀ чⷭ҇тое помышле́нїѧ Бг҃ъ, и҆ пре́жде чре́ва, и҆ пре́же зача́тїемъ вѣ́рному возгла̀ Бж҃ественному Царю̀, ꙗ҆́вѣ, цр҃кви неѡбори́магѡ бы́ти тѧ̀ побо́рника. тѣ́мже прави́лнымъ и҆звѣ́ствомъ Мѵ́ромъ запечатлѣ́нъ є҆сѝ сщ҃еннонача́льства :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* God, knowing the purity of thy mind, even before the womb and before conception, manifestly proclaimed unto the faithful divine Emperor that thou wouldest be an invincible champion of the Church; therefore by canonical testimony wast thou sealed with the myron of the sacred hierarchy.

units.slavonic_incipit: Побѣжда́етъ сѧ ꙗ҆́вѣ и҆ бѣ́дствуетъ собра́нїе
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: беждает ся ве и бедствует собрание полукиндина дланию
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Побѣжда́етъ сѧ ꙗ҆́вѣ и҆ бѣ́дствуетъ собра́нїе Полукінди́на дла́нїю твое́ю, и҆ мꙋ́дрыми твоими гл҃ы, пресла́вне Григо́рїе, Ѳессалони́кскїй первосѣда́телю, и҆ ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆счеза́етъ ды́мъ и҆счезѐ гни́лое безꙋ́мїе, твои́мъ громогла́снымъ и҆ Бг҃осло́внымъ ѧ҆зы́комъ :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* The gathering of Polykindynos[^1253] is manifestly conquered and distressed by thy hand and by thy wise words, O all-glorious Gregory, primate of Thessalonica; and like as smoke vanishes, so is their corrupt folly vanished by thy loud-sounding and theological tongue!

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: бго слово бжие в тебе дво члчкое ество

units.slavonic_incipit: Пѣ́снь, ѳ҃. И҆рмо́съ. Оу҆диви́сѧ оу҆́бѡ ѡ҆
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: песн ф ирмос оудивися оубо о сем радости
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Пѣ́снь, ѳ҃. И҆рмо́съ. Оу҆диви́сѧ оу҆́бѡ ѡ҆ се́мъ: Ра́дости и҆ весе́лїѧ нн҃ѣ, менѐ ра́ди закла́вшемусѧ твоему̀ телцꙋ̀ и҆спо́лни сегѡ̀ ѿ тебѐ ча́ющꙋю мою̀ дш҃ꙋ Бж҃е. заблꙋ́женна прїими́ мѧ, и҆ оу҆мерщвле́нна къ жи́зни возведѝ, и҆ въ Бж҃ественнꙋю ѡ҆де́ждꙋ сп҃снїѧ, в̾ нетлѣ́нїе мѧ̀ ѡ҆блецы̀ :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Ode 9. Heirmos: Be thou amazed now at this (Оудивися убо о сем):* *Troparion:* By Thy calf slain for my sake, fill now with joy and gladness my soul that looks for this from Thee, O God! (Luke 15:23). Receive me who have gone astray, and lead me who was dead back unto life (Luke 15:24, 32), and clothe me in the divine garment of salvation, in incorruption!

units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* O souls who have strayed far from God and are deprived of divine gifts, come fervently, and taking up the repentance of the prodigal, let us cry: O good Father Who art in the heavens, we all have sinned against Thee; cleanse and save them that flee unto Thy mercy!

units.slavonic_incipit: Ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆мы́й млⷭ҇рдїѧ мно́жество мно́гое, не
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: ко имый млрдия множество многое не гнушайся мене
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆мы́й млⷭ҇рдїѧ мно́жество мно́гое, не гнꙋша́йсѧ менѐ Гдⷭ҇и Гдⷭ҇и, въ мно́гихъ сласте́хъ бога́тство и҆жди́вша, и҆ прибѣга́юща нн҃ѣ и҆ зовꙋ́ща блꋋднагѡ гла́сомъ: съгрѣши́х ти сп҃сѝ, прибѣга́ющагѡ мл҃ти твое́й :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* As Thou hast an abundant multitude of tenderheartedness, turn not away in disgust from me, O Lord, O Lord, who have squandered my wealth in many pleasures, but who now flee unto Thee and call with the voice of the prodigal: I have sinned against Thee, save him that flees unto Thy mercy!

units.slavonic_incipit: Сп҃снїѧ приста́нище и҆ наста́вленїе, и҆ предста́телницꙋ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: спсния пристанище и наставление и предстателницу тя имам
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Сп҃снїѧ приста́нище и҆ наста́вленїе, и҆ предста́телницꙋ тѧ̀ и҆́мамъ ра́бъ тво́й, лю́тыхъ всѣ́хъ препѧ́тїй, ꙗ҆́кѡ бл҃га́ѧ къ Бг҃ꙋ мл҃ьбами ти Влⷣчце да и҆зба́влюсѧ, ꙗ҆́кѡ на́ тѧ всю̀ мою̀ наде́ждꙋ возложи́хъ любо́вїю, да вѣ́рою велича́ю тѧ̀ :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Theotokion:* A haven and guidance and protectress of salvation have I, thy servant, obtained thee, that by thy prayers unto God, as thou art good, O Sovereign Lady, I may be delivered from all grievous hindrances; for upon thee have I placed all my hope with love, that in faith I may magnify thee!

units.slavonic_incipit: Зерца́ло Бж҃їе бы́лъ є҆сѝ Григо́рїе, є҆́же
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: зерцало бжие был еси григорие еже по образу
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Зерца́ло Бж҃їе бы́лъ є҆сѝ Григо́рїе, є҆́же по ѡ҆́бразꙋ нескве́рное соблю́лъ є҆сѝ, оу҆ма́ же влⷣкꙋ на стра̑сти плѡтскі̑ѧ мꙋ́жески поста́вивъ, є҆́же по подо́бїю воспрїѧ́лъ є҆сѝ, ѿню́дꙋже до́мъ бы́лъ є҆сѝ Ст҃ы́ѧ Трⷪ҇ца свѣтлѣ́йшїй :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* A divine mirror wast thou, O Gregory, who didst preserve undefiled that which is according to the image; and having manly set the mind as master over carnal passions, thou didst receive that which is according to the likeness, whence thou becamest the most luminous dwelling of the Holy Trinity! (Gen. 1:26).

units.slavonic_incipit: Цр҃ь бл҃гочти́вый, крыла́таго тѧ̀ въздꙋхохо́дна показꙋ́етъ,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: цр блгочтивый крылатаго тя въздухоходна показует сему пособствующа
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Цр҃ь бл҃гочти́вый, крыла́таго тѧ̀ въздꙋхохо́дна показꙋ́етъ, семꙋ̀ посо́бствꙋюща ꙗ҆́кѡ всего̀ и҆спо́лненна бж҃твеннагѡ Дх҃а, на сꙋемꙋ́драго бѣснꙋ́ющагосѧ Варлаа́ма, глаго́лющаго на высотꙋ̀ непра́веднаѧ Бг҃ꙋ, є҆го́же пра́ведно побѣди́лъ є҆сѝ :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* The pious Emperor[^1254] manifests thee as a winged voyager of the air, aiding him as one entirely filled with the Divine Spirit against the vainly wise and raving Barlaam,[^1255] who spoke unrighteous things on high against God (Ps. 72:3, 8 LXX [73:3, 8]); and this heretic didst thou righteously conquer!

units.slavonic_incipit: Бг҃ъ бы́въ, премꙋ́дрости лꙋ́чшїѧ и҆спо́лненъ пресла́вне,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: бг быв премудрости лучшия исполнен преславне свет мирови
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Бг҃ъ бы́въ, премꙋ́дрости лꙋ́чшїѧ и҆спо́лненъ пресла́вне, свѣ́тъ мі́рови просвѣти́лъ є҆сѝ правосла́вїѧ водрꙋзи́въ до́гмата, любо́вїю бо и҆зрѧ́днагѡ любомꙋ́дрїѧ премꙋ́дре, бж҃твенный стра́хъ въ чре́вѣ зача́лъ є҆сѝ, и҆ словеса̀ Дх҃а породи́лъ є҆сѝ :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* Having become a god by deification,[^1256] filled with the higher wisdom, O all-glorious one, thou didst shine forth the light of Orthodoxy unto the world, establishing its dogmas; for through love of the pre-eminent philosophy, O all-wise one, thou didst conceive the divine fear in the womb, and didst bring forth the words of the Spirit! (Isa. 26:18 LXX).

(Isa. 26:18 LXX).

units.slavonic_incipit: Бг҃о: Пѣ́снь ти вѣ́рнїи согла́снѡ прино́симъ,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: бго песн ти вернии согласно приносим блгрения тебе
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Бг҃о: Пѣ́снь ти вѣ́рнїи согла́снѡ прино́симъ, бл҃гре́нїѧ тебѣ̀. ты́ бо дре́внюю раздрꙋши́ла є҆сѝ на́шꙋ клѧ́твꙋ Бг҃ороди́тельнице, и҆ ꙗ҆вле́нїе вси Бж҃твенное оу҆площа́емъ, сп҃снїе, просвѣще́нїе, и҆ млⷭ҇ть тобо́ю, и҆ ра́дость вѣ́чнꙋю :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Theotokion:* A song of thanksgiving do we, the faithful, concordantly offer thee, for thou didst destroy our ancient curse, O Mother of God, and we all reap divine manifestation, salvation, enlightenment, and mercy through thee, and eternal joy!

units.slavonic_incipit: Ра́дꙋйсѧ Ѻ҆тце́мъ похвало̀, ра́дꙋйсѧ Бг҃осло́вѡмъ оу҆ста̀,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: радуйся тцем похвало радуйся бгословом оуста безмолвия селение
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Ра́дꙋйсѧ Ѻ҆тце́мъ похвало̀, ра́дꙋйсѧ Бг҃осло́вѡмъ оу҆ста̀, безмо́лвїѧ селе́нїе, прⷨрости до́ме, оу҆́тлей слы́шателю, пꙋчи́но слове́съ, сло́ва, дѣѧ́нїѧ ѡ҆рга́не, Бг҃овидѣ́нїѧ послꙋ́шателю, и҆сцѣли́телю болѣ́зней чл҃ч҇кихъ, ра́дꙋйсѧ Дх҃а гла́венно, и҆ ме́ртвыхъ и҆ живы́хъ Ѻ҆́ч҃е :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Exapostilarion of the Resurrection. Glory to the Saint, Tone 2, Podoben: "Let us assemble with the disciples" (Оу҆чн҃кѡ́мъ):* Rejoice, boast of the Fathers; rejoice, mouth of the Theologians, habitation of hesychia,[^1257] house of wisdom, listener unto the highest things, abyss of the words of the Word, instrument of action, auditor of the vision of God, healer of human sicknesses; rejoice, chiefest dwelling of the Spirit, and Father of the dead and the living! *Both now: Theotokion: Sovereign Lady of all:*[^1258]

(Matt. 13:8, 23).

units.english_cohort_translation: *At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone, on 6: ...and to the Saint, Ode 3, on 4. After the Entrance, Troparion: Resurrectional, and to the Saint. Glory: Kontakion: to the Saint. Both now: Kontakion in the Triodion. Prokeimenon, Tone 2:* Thou shalt keep us, O Lord: *Verse:* Save me, O Lord, for the godly man ceases: (Ps. 11:8, 2 LXX [12:7, 1]). *The Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 304:* "Thou, Lord, in the beginning didst lay the foundation of the earth..." (Heb. 1:10–2:3). *Alleluia of the current Tone. The Gospel according to Mark, Pericope 7:* "At that time, Jesus entered into Capernaum..." (Mark 2:1–12). *Communion Hymn:* "Praise ye the Lord..." (Ps. 148:1). *And the entire service to the Saint is as is common for a single Hierarch.*[^1260]

units.slavonic_incipit: Безчи́сленаѧ ти съгрѣши́въ, безчи́сленныхъ мꙋ́къ ѡ҆жида́ю,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: безчисленая ти съгрешив безчисленных мук ожидаю скрежета зубнаго
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Безчи́сленаѧ ти съгрѣши́въ, безчи́сленныхъ мꙋ́къ ѡ҆жида́ю, скре́жета зꙋ́бнагѡ, и҆ пла́ча неꙋтѣ́шимагѡ, гее́нны ѡ҆́гненныѧ, и҆ тмы̀ и҆ та́ртара, Сꙋдїѐ првⷣнѣ́йшїй. Сле́зы ми оу҆́бѡ да́рꙋй, и҆́миже ѡ҆брѧ́щꙋ ѡ҆ставле́нїе, и҆ злы́хъ мои́хъ разрѣше́нїе, постѧ́сѧ и҆ зовы́й ти, Влⷣко Хрⷭ҇ѐ оу҆ще́дри мѧ, за вели́кꙋю и҆ бога́тꙋю млⷭ҇ть :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Sticheron 1:* Having sinned innumerably against Thee, I await innumerable torments: the gnashing of teeth, and inconsolable weeping, the Gehenna of fire, darkness, and Tartarus, O most righteous Judge! Grant me, therefore, tears whereby I may find forgiveness and the loosed-bond of my wicked deeds, as I fast and cry unto Thee: O Master Christ, be compassionate unto me, according to Thy great and rich mercy!

units.slavonic_incipit: Менѐ заблꙋ́ждшаго на гора́хъ лю́тыхъ престꙋпле́нїй,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: мене заблуждшаго на горах лютых преступлений взыщи слове
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Менѐ заблꙋ́ждшаго на гора́хъ лю́тыхъ престꙋпле́нїй, взыщи́ Сло́ве, и҆ к̾ себѣ̀ воззовѝ, ѡ҆бы́чаѧ злы́ѧ оу҆ма̀ моегѡ̀ дале́че ѿганѧ́ѧ, оу҆ме́рша па́ки ѡ҆живѝ, и҆ по́стомъ ѡ҆чи́сти, въ пла́чѣ непреста́нномъ вопїю́ща и҆ гл҃юща, Влⷣко Хрⷭ҇ѐ оу҆ще́дри мѧ, за вели́кꙋю и҆ бога́тꙋю млⷭ҇ть :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Sticheron 2:* Seek me out, O Word, who have gone astray upon the mountains of cruel transgressions, and call me back unto Thyself, driving far away the evil customs of my mind; make me alive again who was dead, and cleanse me by fasting, as in unceasing weeping I cry out and say: O Master Christ, be compassionate unto me, according to Thy great and rich mercy!

units.slavonic_incipit: По́ста каче́нше Неде́лю тре́тїю, Трⷪ҇цꙋ чⷭ҇тнꙋ́ю
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: ста каченше неделю третию трцу чтную въсхвалим вернии
units.slavonic_diplomatic: По́ста каче́нше Неде́лю тре́тїю, Трⷪ҇цꙋ чⷭ҇тнꙋ́ю въсхва́лимъ вѣ́рнїи, про́чее ра́достно преходѧ́ще, плотскі̑ѧ же стра̑сти блѧда́ще, ѿ дꙋ́шъ на́шихъ цвѣ́ты бж҃твенныѧ пожне́мъ, вѣнцы̀ и҆спле́тше нача́лници днемъ, да вси Хрⷭ҇а̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ побѣди́телѧ, вѣнцы̀ носѧ́ще воспои́мъ :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Another Sticheron, by Kyr Theodore, Tone the same [Tone 8], Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Пресла́вное):* *Sticheron 3:* Having begun the third week of the Fast, let us praise the precious Trinity, O faithful, joyfully traversing the remainder, and refraining from carnal passions; let us reap divine flowers from our souls, having woven crowns as lords of the day, that we all, wearing crowns, may hymn Christ as Victor! *And in the Menaion, 3. Glory, and now: Theotokion. O Gladsome Light. After the Entrance, the Great Prokeimenon, Tone 8:* Turn not away Thy face: *with its verses* (Ps. 68:18 LXX [69:17]). (see fol. 129 and 194).[^1263]

units.slavonic_incipit: Бра́зды и҆здѣ́левахъ дх҃овныѧ, неосла́бнымъ оу҆мо́мъ, съ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: бразды изделевах дховныя неослабным оумом с скотскими греха
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Бра́зды и҆здѣ́левахъ дх҃овныѧ, неосла́бнымъ оу҆мо́мъ, съ ско́тскими грѣха̀ помышле́нми пожѧ́хъ, всѐ моѐ житїѐ и҆жди́въ блꙋ́днѡ ѡ҆каѧ́нный а҆́зъ, пи́ща лише́нъ оу҆твержда́ющїѧ срⷣце, вре́менною наслажда́ющею сла́стїю насы́тихсѧ. но Ѻ҆́ч҃е бл҃гїй, не затвори́ ми чл҃колю́бныѧ оу҆тро́бы, но ѿве́рзъ прїими́ мѧ, ꙗ҆́кѡ блꙋ́днаго сы́на, и҆ сп҃си́ мѧ :~
units.english_cohort_translation: I cultivated not the spiritual furrows with an unslackening mind, but with bestial thoughts I reaped sin, having prodigally squandered my whole life, wretched that I am; deprived of food that strengthens the heart (Ps. 103:15 LXX [104:15]), I was filled with temporary pleasurable delight. But, O good Father, shut not against me Thy compassions of love for mankind, but open and receive me as the prodigal son, and save me!
units.slavonic_text: Бра́зды и҆здѣ́левахъ дх҃овныѧ, неосла́бнымъ оу҆мо́мъ, съ ско́тскими грѣха̀ помышле́нми пожѧ́хъ, всѐ моѐ житїѐ и҆жди́въ блꙋ́днѡ ѡ҆каѧ́нный а҆́зъ, пи́ща лише́нъ оу҆твержда́ющїѧ срⷣце, вре́менною наслажда́ющею сла́стїю насы́тихсѧ. но Ѻ҆́ч҃е бл҃гїй, не затвори́ ми чл҃колю́бныѧ оу҆тро́бы, но ѿве́рзъ прїими́ мѧ, ꙗ҆́кѡ блꙋ́днаго сы́на, и҆ сп҃си́ мѧ :~

units.slavonic_incipit: Ст҃і: ѡ҆бы́: К̾ тебѣ̀ възведо́хъ ѻ҆́ч҃и
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: сти обы к тебе възведох чи мои мчннции
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Ст҃і: ѡ҆бы́: К̾ тебѣ̀ възведо́хъ ѻ҆́ч҃и моѝ: Мч҃ннцїи Гдⷭ҇ни: И҆ Сла́ва: и҆ нн҃ѣ: Бг҃о: Нб҃наѧ пою́тъ: Зри в̾ нл҃и масопꙋ́стнои. На Ст҃і: Ли́стъ, о҃в. Та́лже ѡ҆б а҆сті́ха, ли́стъ, тнд҃. И҆ про́че послѣ́дованїе ꙗ҆́кѡже оу҆каза́сѧ, на всѧ̑ нл҃ѧ с҃: по́ста, лн҃, рх҃д, и҆ р҃ѳ.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Воздержа́нїѧ ѻ҆гне́мъ, попали́мъ все веще́ное страсте́й воста́нїе, и҆ пла́мень ѻ҆́ный негаси́мый, сле́зными ны́нѣ оу҆гаси́мъ тѡ́ки. Сп҃се мл҃рде Гдⷭ҇и, неѡсꙋжде́нныхъ на́съ соблюдѝ, пода́въ на́мъ съгрѣше́нїемъ проще́нїе :~ в҃. Сла́ва, и҆ нн҃ѣ: Бг҃о:
units.english_cohort_translation: With the fire of abstinence, let us burn up all the material uprising of the passions, and let us now quench that unquenchable flame with streams of tears! units.slavonic_incipit: Бг҃обл҃гтнаѧ чⷭ҇таѧ бл҃гослове́ннаѧ, за млⷭ҇рдїе щедро́тъ,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: бгоблгтная чтая блгословенная за млрдие щедрот из тебе
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Бг҃обл҃гтнаѧ чⷭ҇таѧ бл҃гослове́ннаѧ, за млⷭ҇рдїе щедро́тъ, и҆з̾ тебѐ рожде́ннагѡ, съ вы́шними Си́лами, и҆ съ А҆рха́гг҃лы, и҆ съ всѣ́ми безпло́тными, ѡ҆ на́съ мл҃ѝ, непреста́ннѡ, да́ти на́мъ пре́жде конца̀ проще́нїе, и҆ ѡ҆чище́нїе грѣхѡ́въ, и҆ житїѧ̀ и҆справле́нїе, ꙗ҆́кѡ да ѡ҆́брѧщемъ млⷭ҇ть :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Theotokion:* O Virgin graced of God, pure and blessed, by the tender mercies and compassions of Him Who was born of thee, together with the Hosts on high, and with the Archangels, and with all the Bodiless Hosts, pray unceasingly for us, that before the end He may grant us forgiveness, and cleansing of sins, and amendment of life, so that we may find mercy!

units.slavonic_incipit: Трⷪ҇це ст҃а́ѧ, и҆ чⷭ҇тна́ѧ, по́стъ в̾
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: трце стая и чтная пост в седмицах триех
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Трⷪ҇це ст҃а́ѧ, и҆ чⷭ҇тна́ѧ, по́стъ в̾ Седми́цахъ трїе́хъ препровожда́ющыѧ, сохранѝ цѣ́лы и҆ неѡсꙋжде́нны, сподо́би бл҃го тещѝ и҆ къ про́чїимъ, и҆ всѧ̑ за́повѣди твоѧ̑ соблюстѝ, ꙗ҆́кѡ да си́це дости́гнемъ неѡсꙋжде́ннѡ, ви́дѣти пресла́вное Въскрⷭ҇нїе, пѣ́нїе хва́лꙋ приносѧ́ще :~ в҃. Сла́ва, и҆ нн҃ѣ: Бг҃о:
units.english_cohort_translation: *Sessional Hymn:* O holy and precious Trinity, preserve whole and uncondemned us who are spending the fast in these three weeks; make us worthy to run well unto the remainder also, and to keep all Thy commandments, so that uncondemned we may thus attain to see the all-glorious Resurrection, offering a hymn of praise! *Twice. Glory, and now: Theotokion:*

units.slavonic_incipit: Предста́телнице вѣ́рнымъ Бг҃ороди́телнице, ѡ҆скорблѧ́емымъ ра́дости, и҆
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: предстателнице верным бгородителнице оскорбляемым радости и сетующым превелие
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Предста́телнице вѣ́рнымъ Бг҃ороди́телнице, ѡ҆скорблѧ́емымъ ра́дости, и҆ сѣ́тꙋющымъ преве́лїе оу҆тѣше́нїе, ѿ чре́ва твое́гѡ Дв҃о всест҃а́гѡ преесте́ственнѡ ро́жшагосѧ, непреста́ннѡ ѡ҆ на́съ съ А҆́гг҃лы и҆ нача́лы, молѝ сп҃ти́сѧ на́мъ, в̾ ча́съ и҆спыта́нїѧ, лю́тагѡ ѡ҆сꙋжде́нїѧ :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Theotokion:* O Protectress of the faithful, Mother of God, joy of the afflicted, and great consolation of the mourning: pray unceasingly with the Angels and Principalities unto Him Who was supernaturally born of thy most holy womb, O Virgin, that we may be saved in the hour of trial from cruel condemnation!

units.slavonic_incipit: И҆мѣ́ѧй ꙗ҆́кѡ Бг҃ъ соꙋ́з̾ стра́стное, ка́ющасѧ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: имеяй ко бг соуз страстное кающася приими мя
units.slavonic_diplomatic: И҆мѣ́ѧй ꙗ҆́кѡ Бг҃ъ соꙋ́з̾ стра́стное, ка́ющасѧ прїими́ мѧ, и҆жди́вшагѡ житїѐ моѐ блꙋ́днѡ, вопїю́ти, съгрѣши́хъ, клеветникѡ́въ не тре́бꙋю, стꙋ́дъ дѣ́лъ мои́хъ приносѧ̀ :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Ode 1. Heirmos. Tone 8: Let us send up a song, O ye peoples (Песнь возслем людие):* *Troparion:* Having as God compassionate love,[^1267] receive me who repent, who have prodigally squandered my life, crying unto Thee: I have sinned! I need no accusers, for I bring the shame of mine own deeds!

units.slavonic_incipit: Пи́щꙋ ѡ҆ста́вль А҆́гг҃лскꙋю, оу҆подо́бихсѧ скотѡ́мъ, пита́ѧсѧ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: пищу оставл агглскую оуподобихся скотом питаяся скверною злобою
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Пи́щꙋ ѡ҆ста́вль А҆́гг҃лскꙋю, оу҆подо́бихсѧ скотѡ́мъ, пита́ѧсѧ скве́рною зло́бою, но оу҆́бѡ ѡ҆браща́ющасѧ прїими́ мѧ, ꙗ҆́кѡ є҆ди́наго ѿ наемникъ твои́хъ нб҃ный Ѻ҆́ч҃е :~

units.slavonic_incipit: Нощь страсте́й ѿ пи́ща пребыва́ющꙋю, вси

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Нощь страсте́й ѿ пи́ща пребыва́ющꙋю, вси вѣ́рнїи ѡ҆ста́вльше, свѣ́томъ воздержа́нїѧ то́щнѡ пристꙋ́пимъ, да свѣтоно́сной трапе́зѣ сподо́бимсѧ :~
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* Having forsaken the night of passions that abides from food, let all of us, the faithful let us draw near with zeal by the light of abstinence, that we may be accounted worthy of the light-bearing banquet!

units.slavonic_incipit: Нн҃ѣ в̾ Седми́цахъ трїе́хъ, ꙗ҆́кѡже дре́вле
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: нне в седмицах триех коже древле тридневный иил
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Нн҃ѣ в̾ Седми́цахъ трїе́хъ, ꙗ҆́кѡже дре́вле трїдне́вный І҆и҃ль, ѡ҆чи́стившесѧ бра́тїе, предѣ́лы мл҃твъ дости́гнемъ, и҆ ѿтꙋ́дꙋ Бж҃твенный гла́съ оу҆слы́шавше, Хрⷭ҇а̀ воспои́мъ :~
